E. Power Plant Removal with the Bootstrap Equipment

SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-008-F00 (1) Make sure that the power plant is prepared for removal (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00). 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-010-013-F00 (2) For the thumbnail fairing, do this task: Forward Fairing Removal, TASK 54-52-01-010-801. SUBTASK 71-00-02-980-004-F00 (3) Put the fan cowl panel pins in the strut to keep them away from the engine removal equipment. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-040-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU VISUALLY INSPECT THE BOOTSTRAP KIT BEFORE USE, INSPECT THE LIFT LUGS FOR GOUGES, LINES, OR CRACKS AT THE LUG ROOT AND THE LANYARD HOLES. IF A LUG JOINT OR STRUCTURE IS SUSPECT , THEN REMOVE IT FROM USE. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT INSTALL TAG LINES ON THE GSE AFT BRACKET . TAG LINES ARE THE ROPES THAT YOU ATTACH TO A LOAD TO CONTROL LOAD SPIN AND PENDULAR MOVEMENT . THIS PREVENTS A SIDE-LOAD THE LIFTING LUGS. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (4) Install the forward bootstrap equipment from the bootstrap kit, SPL-2110, as follows (Figure 408): NOTE: The forward bootstrap consists of an inboard arm, an outboard arm, two braces, left and right hand dynamometer assemblies, and two lever hoists. NOTE: In most locations, the lockpins are permanently attached to the bootstrap equipment. (a) Make sure that the inboard arm [143] is on the inboard side and the outboard arm [145] is on the outboard side of the power plant. (b) Use the lockpin [141] to attach the inboard arm [143] to the strut attach fitting. NOTE: The inboard arm has a shear pin below the strut attach fitting to temporarily hold the arm in its correct position. The arm will not fall. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [141]. (c) Use the lockpin [146] to attach the outboard arm [145] to the strut attach fitting. NOTE: The outboard arm also has a shear pin below the strut attach fitting to temporarily hold the arm in its correct position. The arm will not fall. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [146]. (d) Use the lockpin [144] to attach the inboard arm [143] and outboard arm [145] together at the top location. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [144]. (e) Do these steps to install a brace [142] between the inboard arm [143] and strut: NOTE: There are two braces on the forward bootstrap. They consist of a metal rod with a clevis on one end and a permanently attached lockpin at the other end. The two braces are the same. 1) Put the brace [142] aft lockpin in the keyed slot of the inboard arm [143]. 2) Turn the brace [142] 90 degrees until the clevis at the forward end of the brace is aligned with the attach point on the right forward strut. a) Look at the aft side of the inboard arm [143] to make sure that the lockpin has turned and is engaged. 3) Use the lockpin [149] to attach the clevis on the forward end of the brace [142] to the strut. 71-00-02 a) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [149]. (f) Do the above steps again for the other brace [142]. (g) Make sure that the inboard arm [143], outboard arm [145], two braces [142], and all lockpins [141], lockpin [144], lockpin [146], and lockpin [149] are installed correctly. (h) For Engine 1, do these steps: 1) Attach the lever hoist [148] to the outboard arm [145]. WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 2) Make sure that the chains on the lever hoist [148] do not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and the lower block. a) To remove the spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. 3) Attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] to the outboard lever hoist [148] (Figure 409). NOTE: The dynamometer must face forward. To do this, the left dynamometer must be installed upside down. 4) Attach the right hand dynamometer assembly [151] to the inboard arm [143] (Figure 409). NOTE: The dynamometer must face forward. 5) Attach the lever hoist [148] to the right hand dynamometer assembly [151] on the inboard side of the engine. WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 6) Make sure that the chains on the lever hoist [148] do not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and the lower block. a) To remove the spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. 7) Attach the right lower link assembly [150] to the lever hoist [148] (Figure 409). (i) For Engine 2, do these steps: 1) Attach the lever hoist [148] to the inboard arm [143]. 71-00-02 WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 2) Make sure that the chains on the lever hoist [148] do not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and the lower block. a) To remove the spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. 3) Attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] to the inboard lever hoist [148] (Figure 409). NOTE: The dynamometer must face forward. To do this, the left dynamometer must be installed upside down. 4) Attach the right hand dynamometer assembly [151] to the outboard arm [145] (Figure 409). NOTE: The dynamometer must face forward. 5) Attach the lever hoist [148] to the right hand dynamometer assembly [151] on the outboard side of the engine. WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 6) Make sure that the chains on the lever hoist [148] do not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and the lower block. a) To remove the spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. 7) Attach the right lower link assembly [150] to the lever hoist [148] (Figure 409). SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-041-F00 (5) Do these steps to attach the forward bootstrap equipment to the engine (Figure 409): NOTE: The forward bootstrap equipment is attached directly to a cradle-to-engine bracket at the bootstrap attach point on the power plant. (a) Get the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] from the storage box on the cradle assembly. (b) Examine the bolts [162] for signs of damage before the installation. 1) Look at the area from the bolt head to the threads for signs of stretching and necking. 2) Do not use damaged bolts [162]. Replace the bolt if damage is found. (c) Install the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] in the fan case. 1) Make sure that the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] are fully engaged before you install the bolts [162]. 2) Install the bolts [162] to attach the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] to the fan case. 71-00-02 a) Do not use power tools to install the four bolts [162]. b) Tighten the bolts [162] to 70 in-lb (7.91 N·m) - 88 in-lb (9.94 N·m). (d) Attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] to the cradle-to-engine attach bracket [163] (Figure 409). NOTE: An attach fitting is permanently attached to the forward dynamometer. NOTE: The preferred attach fitting is the "banana link", that is a part of the dynamometer assembly. 1) If it is necessary, adjust the length of the lever hoist [148]. 2) Install the lockpin [161]. 3) Attach the safety pin to the lockpin [161]. 4) For the left forward left hand dynamometer assembly [147], make sure that the connector DP0502 is disconnected from the fuel flow transmitter. (e) Attach the right lower link assembly [150] to the engine-to-cradle attach bracket [163] (Figure 409). 1) If it is necessary, adjust the length of the lever hoist [148]. 2) Install the lockpin [161]. 3) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [161]. (f) Use the lever hoists [148] to remove the slack from the forward bootstrap, but do not apply a load on the power plant at this time. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-042-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU VISUALLY INSPECT THE BOOTSTRAP KIT BEFORE USE, INSPECT THE LIFT LUGS FOR GOUGES, LINES, OR CRACKS AT THE LUG ROOT AND THE LANYARD HOLES. IF A LUG JOINT OR STRUCTURE IS SUSPECT , THEN REMOVE IT FROM USE. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT INSTALL TAG LINES ON THE GSE AFT BRACKET . TAG LINES ARE THE ROPES THAT YOU ATTACH TO A LOAD TO CONTROL LOAD SPIN AND PENDULAR MOVEMENT . THIS PREVENTS A SIDE-LOAD THE LIFTING LUGS. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (6) Install the aft bootstrap equipment from the bootstrap kit, SPL-2110, as follows (Figure 410): NOTE: The aft bootstrap consists of two aft support brace [186] and forward support brace [188], a support beam [184], one dynamometer [183] and one lever hoist [182]. The aft bootstrap equipment can only be installed with the lever hoist and dynamometer on the outboard location. (a) Attach the forward support brace [188] to the forward side of the two bootstrap attach brackets [181] on the bottom of the strut. NOTE: The aft support brace [186] and forward support brace [188] must be installed with the longer arm on the outboard side. The location of the braces is opposite between Engine 1 and Engine 2. (b) Attach the other aft support brace [186] to the aft side of the two bootstrap attach brackets [181] on the bottom of the strut. (c) Attach the forward support brace [188] and aft support brace [186] together on the inboard side of the strut with the lockpin assembly [185]. 71-00-02 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin assembly [185]. (d) Slide the support beam [184] in between the two aft support brace [186] and forward support brace [188] until the inboard end engages the inboard lockpin assembly [185]. (e) Attach the support beam [184] to the two aft support braces [186] and forward support brace [188] at the outboard location with the lockpin assembly [187]. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin assembly [187]. (f) Make sure that the two aft support brace [186], forward support brace [188], and support beam [184] are installed correctly. (g) Attach a lever hoist [182] to the end of the support beam [184] with the lockpin [189]. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [189]. WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (h) Make sure that the chain on the lever hoist [182] does not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and the lower block. 1) To remove the spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. (i) Attach a dynamometer [183] to the lever hoist [182]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-043-F00 (7) Do these steps to attach the aft bootstrap equipment to the engine (Figure 411): NOTE: The aft bootstrap equipment is attached directly to the power plant on the outboard side. On Engine 1, the equipment is attached on the left side. On Engine 2, the equipment is attached on the right side. (a) Do these steps to attach the engine attach bracket [202] to the turbine rear frame: 1) Attach the engine attach bracket [202] to the two engine flange bracket [204] and engine flange bracket [205] with the two lockpins [203]. 2) Attach the safety pin to the end of each lockpin [203]. 3) Keep the forward lockpin [203] handle in the up position. (b) Use the lockpin [201] to attach the dynamometer [183] to the engine attach bracket [202]. NOTE: If it is necessary, adjust the length of the lever hoist [182]. 1) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin [201]. (c) Use the lever hoist [182] to remove the slack from the aft bootstrap, but do not apply a load on the power plant at this time. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-044-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU DO ALL THE STEPS GIVEN BELOW TO PREPARE THE DOLLY AND CRADLE ASSEMBLY FOR THE POWER PLANT REMOVAL. IF YOU DO NOT , THE POWER PLANT CAN HIT AND DAMAGE THE PRECOOLER AND STRUT AS IT IS REMOVED. (8) AGSE CRADLE: 71-00-02 Do these steps to prepare the cradle, COM-2118, and base, COM-2111, for the power plant removal (Figure 412): NOTE: After the bootstrap equipment is installed on the airplane, you must use all four persons to remove the power plant. (a) If not already done, remove the diagonal braces from the cradle, COM-2118. 1) To remove the diagonal braces, disconnect the lockpins at each end of the diagonal brace. 2) Put the diagonal braces in their storage position on the base, COM-2111. CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU REMOVE THE EYE-BOLTS BEFORE YOU MOVE THE CRADLE AND DOLLY UNDER THE ENGINE. IF YOU DO NOT , THE EYE- BOLTS CAN HIT THE THRUST REVERSER DURING THE ENGINE REMOVAL. DAMAGE TO THE THRUST REVERSER CAN OCCUR. (b) Remove the eye-bolts from each forward cradle arm. (c) Make sure that the lockpin [221] on each angle bracket [222] is removed. (d) Do these steps to prepare the forward cradle arms: 1) Slide the left trunnion outboard to fully retract it. 2) On the right trunnion, loosen the spanner nut and fully retract the right trunnion outboard. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE TWO FORWARD CRADLE ARMS ARE IN THE OUTBOARD POSITION. IF THEY ARE NOT , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE DOLLY HITS THE POWER PLANT OR INLET . (e) Make sure that the arms on the cradle, COM-2118, are in the outboard position. 1) Remove the lockpins at the bottom of each arm and let the arms pivot out. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-045-F00 (9) F .BROWN CRADLE: Do these steps to prepare the engine cradle, COM-4953, and transportation stand, COM-4954, for the power plant removal (Figure 413): (a) Remove the two transportation arms from the cradle. NOTE: This step is not necessary if the inlet cowl is removed. (b) Lift the rear support arm from the stowage position and rest it against the right side of the cradle. (c) Remove the forward trunnions from their clamps. (d) Put the forward clamp assemblies to the stowed position. 1) Remove the hinge pin and put the clamp assembly to the stowed position. 2) Install the hinge pin. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-046-F00 (10) STANLEY AVIATION CRADLE: Prepare the engine cradle, COM-6276, and transportation stand, COM-6277, for the power plant removal per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-047-F00 (11) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE CRADLE: 71-00-02 Prepare the engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, for the power plant removal per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-048-F00 CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE DOLLY BELOW THE POWER PLANT . DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE DOLLY HITS THE POWER PLANT OR INLET . (12) Put the applicable cradle and base below the power plant. NOTE: Under some ground surface and airplane weight conditions, it could be necessary to lift the airplane to get sufficient clearance between the aft engine mount and the precooler. To get this clearance, extend the main and nose landing gear shock struts with dry air or nitrogen (TASK 12-15-31-610-802). CAUTION MAKE SURE THE CRADLE ARMS DO NOT HIT THE THRUST REVERSERS WHEN YOU MOVE THE CRADLE REARWARD. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) AGSE CRADLE: Put the cradle, COM-2118, and base, COM-2111, in front of the power plant and move it rearward until the cradle is in its correct position under the engine. NOTE: When the cradle is in the correct position, it will not be aligned with the centerline of the engine. The aft end of the cradle will be slightly outboard from a centerline alignment. NOTE: It is very important to align the cradle with the engine. If they are not aligned, it can be difficult to move the engine from the strut to the cradle. 1) If it is necessary, you can use the cradle steering bars to turn the castors. NOTE: This will let the cradle move in a side-to-side movement. (b) F .BROWN CRADLE: Put the engine cradle, COM-4953, and transportation stand, COM-4954, in front of the power plant and move it aft until the cradle is in its correct position below the engine. 1) Use the castor steering arms. 2) Stop when the center of the forward arms are in line with the forward engine-to-cradle attach brackets. 3) Put the forward clamp assemblies to the installation position. a) Remove the hinge pin and put the clamp assembly to the installation position. b) Install the hinge pin and the safety pin. c) Loosen the collar nuts and open the clamp assembly. (c) STANLEY AVIATION CRADLE: Put the engine cradle, COM-6276, and transportation stand, COM-6277, in its correct position under the engine per the vendor manual. (d) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE CRADLE: Put the engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, in its correct position under the engine per the vendor manual. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-030-F00 (13) Before you apply a load to the bootstrap equipment, make sure that all dynamometers are set to the zero position. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-049-F00 CAUTION DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 3850 POUNDS (1746 KG) TO THE FORWARD INBOARD DYNAMOMETER, 3350 POUNDS (1520 KG) TO THE FORWARD OUTBOARD DYNAMOMETER AND 1300 POUNDS (590 KG) TO THE AFT DYNAMOMETER. IF YOU APPLY MORE THAN THE LIMITS, DAMAGE TO THE POWER PLANT , WING AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION ONE PERSON MUST OBSERVE EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN THE LEVER HOISTS ARE OPERATED. LOADS THAT ARE CHANGED AT ONE HOIST CAN AFFECT THE LOADS AT OTHER HOIST LOCATIONS. BECAUSE OF THIS, THE LOADS CAN GO ABOVE THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS IF NOT MONITORED CAREFULLY . (14) Apply a load to the lever hoists as follows: (a) Apply a load to the lever hoists until each dynamometer reads as follows: NOTE: The load values given below include the necessary preload force and the weight of the engine. 1) Forward dynamometers for the No. 1 powerplant: a) The right hand dynamometer assembly [151] (inboard) reads 3700 ±100 lb (1678 ±45 kg). b) The left hand dynamometer assembly [147] (outboard) reads 3200 ±100 lb (1451 ±45 kg). 2) Forward dynamometers for the No. 2 powerplant: a) The left hand dynamometer assembly [147] (inboard) reads 3700 ±100 lb (1678 ±45 kg). b) The right hand dynamometer assembly [151] (outboard) reads 3200 ±100 lb (1451 ±45 kg). 3) The aft dynamometer [183] reads 1100 ±100 lb (499 ±45 kg). SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-036-F00 (15) Disconnect the forward engine mounts as follows (Figure 414): (a) Loosen all four forward mount bolts [241] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use an 11/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts. (b) Remove the four forward mount bolts [241]. 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [241]. 2) Remove the washers [244]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-037-F00 (16) Disconnect the aft engine mounts as follows (Figure 415): (a) Loosen all four aft mount bolts [263] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use a 15/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts [263]. 71-00-02 (b) Remove the four aft engine mount bolts [263]. 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [263]. (c) Remove the washers [262]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-038-F00 CAUTION WHEN YOU LOWER THE ENGINE, MAKE SURE THAT ALL TUBES, WIRES AND DUCTS BETWEEN THE STRUT AND ENGINE ARE DISCONNECTED. DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE AFT END OF THE ENGINE IS ALWAYS HIGHER THAN THE FRONT . IF IT IS NOT , THE FIRE SHIELD ON THE FAN COWL SUPPORT BEAM CAN HIT THE INLET COWL. DAMAGE TO THE FIRE SHIELD CAN OCCUR. (17) Do these steps to lower the power plant into the applicable cradle (Figure 416, Figure 417): (a) Slowly decrease the load on the two lever hoists [148] and lever hoist [182] until the engine mounts are free of the shear pins [242] and shear pin [264]. (b) Carefully monitor the power plant to make sure that all disconnects and separation points have been made. (c) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG: Make sure that the interference pin at the 12 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf does not touch the aft strut while you lower the engine. (d) When the engine is free of the separation points and disconnect locations, turn the engine in the horizontal direction until it is parallel to the ground. (e) AGSE CRADLE: Do these steps to engage the engine with the cradle (Figure 412): 1) Lower the engine into the cradle until the forward cradle arms can swing back to the vertical position with the trunnions clear. 2) Install the lower lockpins which hold the forward arms in the vertical position. 3) Examine and re-position the stand if necessary to align the trunnion shafts with the cradle-to-engine attach bracket [163]. a) If the trunnions are aligned with the brackets, lock the wheel castors on the cradle. 4) Slide the left trunnion into the cradle-to-engine attach bracket [163] until it is fully engaged. a) Install the lockpin [221] and lockpin [224]. 5) Slide the right trunnion into the cradle-to-engine attach bracket [163] until it is fully engaged. a) Install the lockpin [221] and lockpin [224]. 6) Continue to lower the aft end of the engine until you can engage the aft support arm with the clevis on the Turbine Rear Frame (TRF). a) Install the lockpin [281] to attach the support arm to the TRF . 71-00-02 7) With the engine still be suspended by the bootstrap, adjust the engine position to make sure that the bottom of the trunnion mounts are in full contact with the angle bracket [222] along the full length of the angle bracket. 8) Insert the adjustment gage [223]. NOTE: The adjustment gage should close to touch the retainer plate. 9) Thread the right forward arm spanner nut outboard until it rests against the angle bracket. a) Tighten the spanner nut with the wrench to force the forward cradle arms outboard to restrict deflection. b) Make sure that the left trunnion is indexed against the pin while you adjust the spanner nut. c) Lock the spanner nut with the set screw. CAUTION ADJUST THE RIGHT TRUNNION UNTIL THE PIN FULLY ENGAGES FOR THE LEFT AND RIGHT TRUNNION. IF IT DOES NOT FULLY ENGAGE, THE CRADLE WILL NOT HOLD THE ENGINE IF THE LATERAL LOADS BECOME HIGH. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 10) Make sure that the trunnions are adjusted correctly. a) The bottom of the trunnion mounts are in full contact with the angle bracket [222] along the full length of the angle bracket. b) If unpinned, the trunnions slide in and out. c) The four cap screw heads should have an approximate gap of 0.01 in. (0.254 mm) under each head and lockwire installed. 11) Tighten the collar on the aft mount support arm and tighten the set screw. (f) F .BROWN CRADLE: Do these steps to engage the engine with the cradle (Figure 413): 1) Lower the engine until the forward engine-to-cradle attach bracket [163] is approximately 2 in. (50.80 mm) above the forward clamps on the cradle. 2) Install the forward trunnions into the uniball sockets located at the center of the forward engine-to-cradle attach bracket [163]. 3) Continue to lower the engine until the trunnions go in the bottom of the forward clamps. 4) As each trunnion reaches a horizontal position, do these steps to lock the clamps: a) Close the top clamp over the trunnions. b) Put the swing bolts in the lock position and tighten the collar nuts. c) Tighten the collar nuts to 50 ft-lb (67.8 N·m). d) Make sure that the end of the trunnions are correctly installed in the uniball sockets. 5) Continue to lower the aft end until you can engage the support arm with the clevis on the turbine rear frame. a) Use a lockpin to attach the support arm to the turbine rear frame. b) Attach the safety pin to the end of the lockpin. 71-00-02 (g) STANLEY AVIATION CRADLE: Engage the engine with the cradle per the vendor manual. (h) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE CRADLE: Engage the engine with the cradle per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-039-F00 (18) Do these steps to disconnect the bootstrap equipment from the power plant (Figure 409, Figure 411): (a) For the forward bootstrap equipment, remove the lockpins [161] that attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] and right lower link assembly [150] to the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163]. (b) For the aft bootstrap equipment, remove the lockpin [201] that attaches the dynamometer [183] to the engine attach bracket [202]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-040-F00 (19) Do these steps to remove the seal from the top of the engine pneumatic duct and the starter duct. NOTE: Keep the seals for the installation. (a) Remove the seal [123] from the top of the engine pneumatic duct (Figure 407). (b) Remove the seal [62] from the starter duct (Figure 404). (c) Install protective covers on the openings on the precooler control valve, precooler, engine pneumatic and starter ducts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-041-F00 (20) Remove the power plant from the work area (Figure 417). CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE POWER PLANT AWAY FROM THE AIRPLANE. DAMAGE TO THE THRUST REVERSERS AND POWER PLANT CAN OCCUR IF THE POWER PLANT HITS THE THRUST REVERSERS. (a) To remove the power plant, move it forward until it is free of the thrust reversers. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-031-F00 (21) Remove the two lockpins [203] and engine attach bracket [202] from the turbine rear frame (Figure 411). SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-032-F00 (22) If it is necessary, remove the bootstrap equipment from the strut (Figure 408, Figure 410). SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-033-F00 (23) If you move the engine, do these steps: (a) AGSE CRADLE: Install the eye-bolt for the diagonal brace on the forward cradle arms. (b) Install the diagonal brace on the forward cradle arms.

71-00-02-000-803-F00Power Plant - Removal with the Cobra Engine Change System ATA 71 · Task 000-803-F00

Task Description

4. Power Plant - Removal with the Cobra Engine Change System

A. General

(1) This task has the steps to remove power plant with the Cobra engine change system. (a) Do not do other procedures on the airplane that will cause the airplane to change weight or height. NOTE: These procedures can apply loads to the pylon strut that will be more than the permitted preload limits. 1) Examples of these procedures are: • If you add or remove an item to or from the airplane, that changes the weight of the airplane. • If you change the Center of Gravity (CG) of the airplane, or airplane-to-ground level position. • If you do a maintenance procedure, that causes the airplane to move.

B. References

Reference Title 08-21-02-580-801 Level the Airplane With a Plumb Bob and Inclinometers (P/B 201) 08-21-03-580-801 Make the Airplane Level (P/B 201) 12-15-31-610-802 Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Servicing, Airplane on the Ground (P/B 301) 54-52-01-010-801 Forward Fairing Removal (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description COM-17619 Digital Inclinometer; Range of +/- 45 degrees; Resolution of 0.01 degrees. Part #: 137-2165-01 Supplier: 64790 Part #: 54-635-601-0 Supplier: 1E258 SPL-14956 Cradle - Engine Transportation, Air/Truck, CFM56-7 (Cradle D71CRA00005G02 is included in Stand D71STA00005G02) Part #: D71STA00005G02 Supplier: F4590 SPL-14957 Trolley - Engine Transportation, Air/Truck, CFM56-7 (Trolley D71TRO00005G03 is included in Stand D71STA00005G02) Part #: D71STA00005G02 Supplier: F4590 SPL-15141 Lifting Adapter - Cobra Part #: TPBAC0B0 Supplier: 1JJE1 SPL-15143 Engine Change System - Cobra Part #: TP91-G Supplier: 1JJE1 SPL-19148 Lifting Beam - Cobra Part #: TPBBC* Supplier: 1JJE1 Opt Part #: TPBBC0A0 Supplier: 1JJE1 Opt Part #: TPBBC0B0 Supplier: 1JJE1 71-00-02 (Continued) Reference Description SPL-19149 Lifting Lug - Cobra Part #: TPBLA0B0 Supplier: 1JJE1 SPL-23691 Tool - Removal/Installation, Beam STD-11729 Plumb Bob STD-23306 Level - Laser

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

E. Power Plant Removal with the Cobra Engine Change System

NOTE: The engine trolley, SPL-14957, and engine cradle, SPL-14956, are approved engine stand for using the Cobra system, SPL-15143. To designate a dolly consisting of the engine trolley, SPL-14957, and engine cradle, SPL-14956, the term “engine stand” is used in the procedure. SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-016-F00 (1) Make sure that the power plant is prepared for removal (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00). SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-021-F00 WARNING DO NOT DO A PROCEDURE DURING THE ENGINE CHANGE THAT WILL CAUSE THE AIRPLANE TO CHANGE WEIGHT OR HEIGHT . THE CHANGE IN WEIGHT AND HEIGHT CAN CHANGE THE PRELOAD APPLIED AGAINST THE PYLON STRUT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (2) Do not do other procedures on the airplane that will cause the airplane to change weight or height. NOTE: These procedures can apply loads to the pylon strut that will be more than the permitted preload limits. (a) Do not do other procedures on the airplane until you lower the engine on the ground. SUBTASK 71-00-02-800-010-F00 (3) Use Table 403 for the approved engine stand and applicable upward loads (preload) for the Cobra system, SPL-15143. NOTE: Cobra Engine Change System uses the term "preload". This term represents the compressive load between the pylon and the engine mounts. Table 403/71-00-02-993-822-F00 Approved Engine Stand and Preload Engine Stand Additional Load Applied to FWD Fork Tube (lb) Additional Load Applied to AFT Fork Tube (lb) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE engine stand D71STA00005G02 (engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957) 579 1121 SUBTASK 71-00-02-580-008-F00 (4) Make sure that the airplane is level and stable. 71-00-02 (a) If it is necessary, do one of these tasks: • Level the Airplane With a Plumb Bob and Inclinometers, TASK 08-21-02-580-801 • Make the Airplane Level, TASK 08-21-03-580-801. SUBTASK 71-00-02-010-018-F00 (5) For the thumbnail fairing, do this task: Forward Fairing Removal, TASK 54-52-01-010-801. SUBTASK 71-00-02-980-006-F00 (6) Put the fan cowl panel pins in the strut to keep them away from the engine removal equipment. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-067-F00 (7) Prepare the engine trolley, SPL-14957, and engine cradle, SPL-14956, for the power plant removal per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-017-F00 (8) Refer to the Cobra Engine Change System Manual for the detailed instructions for the preparation and use of the tool. SUBTASK 71-00-02-580-009-F00 (9) Make sure that there is sufficient clearance to put the engine stand in its position under the engine. SUBTASK 71-00-02-800-011-F00 (10) Make a center line for the engine stand on the floor as follows: (a) Use the plumb bob, STD-11729, or leveling laser, STD-23306, to mark a location on the floor directly under the center of the engine spinner. (b) Draw a straight line between the marks. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-045-F00 (11) Use the beam removal/installation tool, SPL-23691, to install the lifting beam, SPL-19148, into the engine stand. (a) Make sure that the lifting beam, SPL-19148, extend equal distance from the engine stand at both sides. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-068-F00 CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE DOLLY BELOW THE POWER PLANT . DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE DOLLY HITS THE POWER PLANT OR INLET . (12) Put the engine stand in its correct position under the engine per the vendor manual. NOTE: Under some ground surface and airplane weight conditions, it could be necessary to lift the airplane to get sufficient clearance between the aft engine mount and the precooler. To get this clearance, extend the main and nose landing gear shock struts with dry air or nitrogen (TASK 12-15-31-610-802). (a) Locate the engine stand center line 3.5 in. (8.9 cm) outboard from the engine center line. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-069-F00 (13) Connect the Cobra system, SPL-15143 to the engine as follows: (a) Connect the lifting adapters, SPL-15141, to the lifting beams, SPL-19148. (b) Connect the lifting adapters, SPL-15141, to the engine stand tie-down rings with the tie-down straps. 71-00-02 (c) Position the primary and secondary units of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, on both sides of the engine stand. 1) Make sure that the primary unit is on the outboard side of the engine. 2) Make sure that the secondary unit is on the inboard side of the engine. (d) Connect the lifting lugs, SPL-19149, to the lifting adapters, SPL-15141. (e) Connect the lifting lug, SPL-19149, to the primary and secondary units of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. 1) Refer to Cobra Engine Change System Manual for the correct set up of these parts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-046-F00 (14) Use the Cobra Engine Change System Manual to prepare the Cobra system, SPL-15143, as follows: (a) Connect all hydraulic and electrical connections between the primary and secondary units. (b) Activate external electrical power to the primary unit of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. (c) Adjust the two units to make sure that they are in the neutral position at the transversal and lateral movement axis. (d) Adjust the two units to make sure that the crossbeams and the load cells are in the correct positions. (e) If there is not a built-in inclinometer on the Cobra system, SPL-15143, install the digital inclinometer, COM-17619, on the engine cradle, SPL-14956, parallel to the ground. SUBTASK 71-00-02-800-012-F00 (15) Use the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, to select the correct load sheet for the engine and engine stand configuration. (a) Make sure that the load sheet is applicable to the engine that will be removed and engine stand configuration. (b) Use this table for approved engines stands and applicable upward loads (preload) for using the Cobra Engine Change System: Table 403. NOTE: The Cobra Engine Change System uses the term "preload". This term represents the compressive load between the pylon and the engine mounts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-070-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT NO PERSONNEL ARE BELOW THE ENGINE WHEN THE COBRA SYSTEM IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (16) Do these steps to attach the engine stand to the engine: (a) Use the Cobra system, SPL-15143, to slowly lift the engine stand to the engine. (b) Stop operation after you lift the engine stand approximately 2 in. (5.1 cm) - 3 in. (7.6 cm) from the ground. (c) Tighten the tie-down straps again. 1) Make sure that the lifting beams, SPL-19148, do not move. (d) Rotate the engine stand approximately 5.5 - 6 degrees. 1) If it is necessary, use the digital inclinometer, COM-17619, or built-in inclinometer to measure the rotation. 71-00-02 (e) Make sure that you monitor the clearances between the engine and the nacelle surfaces. (f) Make sure that you monitor the clearances between the stand and the ground. (g) Slowly lift the engine stand, until it is approximately 3 in. (7.6 cm) below the engine. (h) If personnel needs to be on the engine stand during the engine removal, make sure that they are on the engine stand before the ZERO OUT function is actuated. 1) Make sure that the digital inclinometer, COM-17619, or built-in inclinometer is activated. (i) Use the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, to select the ZERO OUT function. NOTE: The values on the main screen represents the additional load values on the pillars, which contributes to the preload values on each mount after activating the ZERO OUT function. NOTE: After selecting the ZERO OUT function, the actual weight on the Cobra system, SPL-15143, will be tared out. 1) Make sure that no part of the engine stand is in contact with the engine or aircraft when you actuate the ZERO OUT function. (j) Engage the engine with the engine cradle, SPL-14956, per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-800-013-F00 CAUTION DO NOT LET MORE THAN PERMITTED WEIGHT ON THE FORWARD AND AFT SIDES. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE AND ENGINE SUPPORT EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (17) Use the Cobra system, SPL-15143, to slowly lift the engine stand until the necessary preload is achieved at all four pillars on the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. (a) Select the Automatic Preload Maintaining (APM) mode on the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. 1) Make sure that the necessary preload is displayed at all four pillars on the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, before the APM mode is activated. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-047-F00 (18) Disconnect the forward engine mounts as follows (Figure 414): (a) Loosen all four forward mount bolts [241] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use an 11/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts. (b) Remove the four forward mount bolts [241]. 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [241]. 2) Remove the washers [244]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-048-F00 (19) Disconnect the aft engine mounts as follows (Figure 415): (a) Loosen all four aft mount bolts [263] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use a 15/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts. (b) Remove the four aft engine mount bolts [263]. 71-00-02 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [263]. (c) Remove the washers [262]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-049-F00 CAUTION WHEN YOU LOWER THE ENGINE, MAKE SURE THAT ALL TUBES, WIRES AND DUCTS BETWEEN THE STRUT AND ENGINE ARE DISCONNECTED. DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE AFT END OF THE ENGINE IS ALWAYS HIGHER THAN THE FRONT . IF IT IS NOT , THE FIRE SHIELD ON THE FAN COWL SUPPORT BEAM CAN HIT THE INLET COWL. DAMAGE TO THE FIRE SHIELD CAN OCCUR. (20) Use the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, to lower the engine and the engine stand to the ground as follows: (a) At the mobile panel of the Cobra system, SPL-15143, deactivate the APM mode. (b) Slowly lower the engine and the engine stand down until the engine mounts are free of the shear pins [242] and shear pin [264]. (c) Carefully monitor the power plant to make sure that all disconnects and separation points have been made. (d) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG; Make sure that the interference pin at the 12 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf does not touch the aft strut while you lower the engine. (e) When the engine is free of the separation points and disconnect locations, rotate the engine and the engine stand in the horizontal direction until the digital inclinometer, COM-17619, or built-in inclinometer reads ZERO. 1) Make sure that you monitor the clearances between the engine and nacelle surfaces. 2) Make sure that you monitor the clearances between the engine stand and the ground. (f) Slowly lower the engine and the engine stand down until the stand is on the ground. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-050-F00 (21) Do these steps to remove the seal from the top of the engine pneumatic duct and the starter duct. NOTE: Keep the seals for the installation. (a) Remove the seal [123] from the top of the engine pneumatic duct (Figure 407). (b) Remove the seal [62] from the starter duct (Figure 404). (c) Install protective covers on the openings on the precooler control valve, precooler, engine pneumatic and starter ducts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-051-F00 (22) Do these steps to move the engine stand away from the airplane: (a) Make sure that the pillars are completely retracted. (b) Turn off external electrical power to the primary unit of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. 71-00-02 (c) Disconnect and stow all electrical and hydraulic lines between the primary and secondary units of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. (d) Disconnect the lifting lugs, SPL-19149, from the primary and secondary units of the Cobra system, SPL-15143. (e) Move the primary and secondary units away from the engine stand. (f) Remove the lifting lugs, SPL-19149, from the lifting adapters, SPL-15141. (g) Remove the lifting adapters, SPL-15141, from the lifting beams, SPL-19148. (h) Carefully move the engine stand with the engine until it is clear of the airplane. (i) Remove the lifting beams, SPL-19148, from the engine stand using the beam removal/installation tool, SPL-23691. SUBTASK 71-00-02-560-004-F00 (23) If you move the engine, install the diagonal brace on the forward cradle arms. SUBTASK 71-00-02-860-035-F00 (24) Put the covers on the open ends of the ducts on the engine and strut.

5. Power Plant - Removal with the JacXson U70

A. General

(1) This task has the steps to remove power plant with the JacXson U70.

B. References

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine 71-00-02

E. Power Plant Removal with the JacXson U70

SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-009-F00 (1) Make sure that the power plant is prepared for removal (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00). SUBTASK 71-00-02-010-014-F00 (2) Open the left and right thrust reversers on the applicable engine (TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00). SUBTASK 71-00-02-010-015-F00 (3) For the thumbnail fairing, do this task: Forward Fairing Removal, TASK 54-52-01-010-801. SUBTASK 71-00-02-980-005-F00 (4) Put the fan cowl panel pins in the strut to keep them away from the engine removal equipment. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-074-F00 (5) Prepare the engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, for the power plant removal per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-010-F00 WARNING OBEY THE JACXSON U70 USER MANUAL WHEN YOU OPERATE THE JACXSON U70. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE A GOOD VIEW OF THE EQUIPMENT AND PERSONNEL WHEN YOU OPERATE THE JACXSON U70. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (6) Use the JACXSON U70 User Manual for the detailed instructions for the preparation and use of the JACXSON U70 during the engine removal procedure. SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-011-F00 (7) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control in the CONFIGURE mode to set the engine and engine stand configurations. (a) Select the option applicable to the engine, engine stand, and inlet or no inlet configuration. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-051-F00 (8) Make sure that the JACXSON U70 FWD forks are at position 1. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-075-F00 (9) Make sure that the JACXSON U70 AFT forks are at position 25. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-076-F00 (10) Make sure that the fork heights use the two middle pin hole locations as defined in the CONFIGURE mode of the remote control. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-052-F00 CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE DOLLY BELOW THE POWER PLANT . DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE DOLLY HITS THE POWER PLANT OR INLET . (11) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to pick up and maneuver engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, below the power plant. NOTE: Under some ground surface and airplane weight conditions, it could be necessary to lift the airplane to get sufficient clearance between the aft engine mount and the precooler. To get this clearance, extend the main and nose landing gear shock struts with dry air or nitrogen (TASK 12-15-31-610-802). (a) Put the engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, in front of the power plant and move it rearward until the cradle is in its correct position under the engine. (b) Record the values of the engine stand. NOTE: The values are used when applying preload. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-053-F00 (12) Do these steps to lift the engine trolley, SPL-14957, and attach the engine cradle, SPL-14956, to the engine: (a) Make sure that you continuously monitor the distance between the JACXSON U70 work platform, engine, and thrust reversers for possible interference while you lift the engine stand. (b) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to raise the engine trolley, SPL-14957, until it is approximately 4 in. (10 cm) - 6 in. (15 cm) below the engine. (c) Engage the engine with the engine cradle, SPL-14956, per user manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-054-F00 CAUTION MONITOR THE LOADS ON THE LOAD MONITOR. MAKE SURE THAT THE LOADS ARE LESS THEN THE LIMITS. IF THE LOADS ARE MORE THAN THE LIMITS, DAMAGE TO THE STRUT AND ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT REFUEL OR MAKE CHANGES TO THE AIRCRAFT WEIGHT OR THE CENTER OF GRAVITY (COG) WHILE YOU APPLY PRELOADS TO THE ENGINE. DO NOT REFUEL, CHANGE THE AIRCRAFT WEIGHT , OR CHANGE THE COG. MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT INCREASE THE PRELOADS MORE THAN MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE WEIGHT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO THE STRUT , THE ENGINE, OR SUPPORT EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (13) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to apply an extra allowable load to the engine until the load monitor show approximately but no more than these extra allowable loads. 71-00-02 (a) Make sure that the combined forward and combined aft loads do not exceed the stated loads below. NOTE: The load values given below include the necessary preload force and the weight of the engine. NOTE: The load values below are added to the load of the empty stand recorded earlier. NOTE: The loads must be determined without personnel standing on the lifting platforms of the JacXson U70. 1) Loads without inlet: a) 4000 lb (1814 kg) - total (outboard and inboard) forward load. b) 4500 lb (2041 kg) - total (outboard and inboard) aft load. 2) Loads with inlet: a) 4400 lb (1996 kg) - total (outboard and inboard) forward load. b) 4500 lb (2041 kg) - total (outboard and inboard) aft load. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-042-F00 (14) Disconnect the forward engine mounts as follows (Figure 414): (a) Loosen all four forward mount bolts [241] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use an 11/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts. (b) Remove the four forward mount bolts [241]. 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [241]. 2) Remove the washers [244]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-043-F00 (15) Disconnect the aft engine mounts as follows (Figure 415): (a) Loosen all four aft mount bolts [263] one-half turn until you see a clearance under the bolt heads. NOTE: Use a 15/16-inch socket to loosen the bolts [263]. (b) Remove the four aft engine mount bolts [263]. 1) Make sure that the engine mount surfaces continue to touch the strut mating surfaces as you remove the bolts [263]. (c) Remove the washers [262]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-044-F00 CAUTION WHEN YOU LOWER THE ENGINE, MAKE SURE THAT ALL TUBES, WIRES AND DUCTS BETWEEN THE STRUT AND ENGINE ARE DISCONNECTED. DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE AFT END OF THE ENGINE IS ALWAYS HIGHER THAN THE FRONT . IF IT IS NOT , THE FIRE SHIELD ON THE FAN COWL SUPPORT BEAM CAN HIT THE INLET COWL. DAMAGE TO THE FIRE SHIELD CAN OCCUR. (16) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to lower the engine as follows: 71-00-02 (a) Slowly decrease the load on the JACXSON U70 until the engine mounts are free of the shear pins [242] and shear pin [264]. (b) Carefully monitor the power plant to make sure that all disconnects and separation points have been made. (c) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG; Make sure that the interference pin at the 12 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf does not touch the aft strut while you lower the engine. (d) When the engine is free of the separation points and disconnect locations, operate the joystick on the remote control for the lift, tilt, and roll management to turn the engine in the horizontal direction until it is parallel to the ground. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-045-F00 (17) Do these steps to remove the seal from the top of the engine pneumatic duct and the starter duct. NOTE: Keep the seals for the installation. (a) Remove the seal [123] from the top of the engine pneumatic duct (Figure 407). (b) Remove the seal [62] from the starter duct (Figure 404). (c) Install protective covers on the openings on the precooler control valve, precooler, engine pneumatic and starter ducts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-034-F00 (18) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to carefully maneuver the engine on the engine stand away from the aircraft. (a) Make sure that you monitor the clearance between the engine and other components while you pull the engine stand forward. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-036-F00 (19) Use the JACXSON U70 remote control to disengage the JACXSON U70 from the engine trolley, SPL-14957. SUBTASK 71-00-02-860-031-F00 (20) Put the covers on the open ends of the ducts on the engine and strut.

Prepare for the Installation SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-015-F00 (1) Do these steps for the applicable engine: (a) Do this task: INTERNAL - GENERAL VISUAL: LEFT STRUT FORWARD AND AFT ENGINE MOUNT TO STRUT SHEAR PINS, TASK 54-05-03-210-805. 71-00-02 (b) Do this task: INTERNAL - GENERAL VISUAL: RIGHT STRUT FORWARD AND AFT ENGINE MOUNT TO STRUT SHEAR PINS, TASK 54-05-03-210-806. SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-010-F00 (4) Make sure that the configuration of the engine to be installed is compatible with the airplane and thrust reversers. NOTE: If the engine of a different configuration is installed, the procedure of intermix is required in accordance with POWER PLANT (ENGINE INTERMIX), SUBJECT 71-00-07. (a) Refer to the applicable Boeing Service Bulletin for the installation procedure and concurrent requirements necessary for each of the CFM56-7B series engine (Table 404). NOTE: The newest version of the CFM56-7B series engine is the CFM56-7BEXX engine. The “XX” in CFM56-7BXX/3 is the thrust rating of the engine. This information is found on the engine data placard on the engine fan case (Figure 421). NOTE: A T ech Insertion (TI) engine has a “/3” after the thrust rating on the engine data plate. An example of a Singular Annular Combustor (SAC) Engine with TI is CFM56-7B22/3. An example of a non-TI engine is CFM56-7B22. The “XX” in CFM56-7BXX/3 is the thrust rating of the engine. This information is found on the engine data placard on the engine fan case (Figure 421). NOTE: In Table 404, “NONE” indicates that the engine type is the initial delivery configuration for the corresponding airplane line number. If an airplane engine configuration changes to its initial engine installation configuration, use an equivalent opposite procedure for the engine currently installed. For example, if an airplane (line position, 3700-9999) had CFM56-7BEXX engine when delivered, then the CFM56-7BEXX engine replaces the previously installed intermixed CFM56-7BXX SAC engine, refer to the service bulletin 71-1658. This pin engages in a mating receptacle on the bottom of the aft strut. If the mating receptacle is not found on the strut, the strut is not compatible with the exhaust nozzle. You must install the long exhaust nozzle and long exhaust plug on this engine. (a) For the compatible configuration refer to Table 405. Table 405/71-00-02-993-820-F00 AIRPLANE LINE POSITION SB 737-54-1047 INCORPORATION LONG NOZZLE AND LONG PLUG SHORT NOZZLE AND SHORT PLUG 0001-3761 PRE-SB PERMITTED NOT PERMITTED 0001-3761 POST-SB PERMITTED PERMITTED 3762-9999 POST BY PRR NOT PERMITTED PERMITTED SUBTASK 71-00-02-860-010-F00 (6) If it is not already done, do this topic: Prepare for the Removal. SUBTASK 71-00-02-900-001-F00 (7) Do these steps to install the compression rod assembly [110] on the 12:00 o'clock strut of the replacement engine (Figure 406): NOTE: If you re-install the same engine or if the replacement engine has a compression rod installed, this step is not necessary. The compression rod assembly is installed loosely in the bracket with the thrust reverser open. When the thrust reverser closes, the receiver cups capture the rod and moves the rod to the center of the receiver cups. (a) For compression rods with stop rings, do these steps to remove the compression rod assembly [110] from the removed engine: RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPRESSION ROD ASSEMBLY P/N 315A2080-1 1) To remove one of the stop rings, remove the two bolts on a ring half. RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPRESSION ROD ASSEMBLY P/N 315A2080-4 2) Move one of the stop rings to the center of the compression rod. RYR ALL 71-00-02 3) Remove the rod assembly from the bracket. RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPRESSION ROD ASSEMBLY P/N 315A2080-1 (b) To install the compression rod assembly [110] on the replacement engine, do these steps: 1) Put the rod assembly (with one stop ring installed) in the bracket. 2) Loosely install the removed stop ring on the compression rod with the two bolts. 3) Apply sealant, A00160, between the stop ring and compression rod and to the threads of the two bolts. 4) Torque the two bolts to 22.5 ±2.5 in-lb (2.5 ±0.3 N·m). RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPRESSION ROD ASSEMBLY P/N 315A2080-4 (c) To install the compression rod assembly [110] on the replacement engine, do these steps: 1) Put the rod assembly in the bracket. 2) Move the stop ring away from the center of the compression rod. RYR ALL SUBTASK 71-00-02-230-001-F00 (8) Use the same forward mount bolts [241], barrel nuts [243], aft mount bolts [263], or barrel nuts [261] again, do this task: Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (Water Washable), TASK 70-40-01-910-801-F00 or Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (Portable Post-Emulsifiable), TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00. NOTE: This inspection is necessary if it is the operator's policy to use the mount bolts or barrel nuts again. NOTE: This inspection is not necessary if the operator uses new mount bolts and barrel nuts. (a) Discard the forward mount bolts [241] and aft mount bolts [263] with damage that you can feel with a fingernail or thread damage you can see. 1) If there is damage (nicks/dents) on the forward mount bolts [241] and aft mount bolts [263], discard these bolts. SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-003-F00 (9) Do the self-locking check on the four barrel nuts [243] of the forward engine mount (Figure 414). (a) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the bolts [241]. (b) Make sure that the locking torque on the barrel nuts [243] is between 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m). NOTE: Apply only the torque in the above torque range to prevent wear on the barrel nut threads. It is not necessary to find the breakaway torque. (c) If the self-locking torque on the barrel nuts [243] is not between 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m), replace the barrel nuts [243]. (d) Make sure that the retainers do not have cracks or damage. (e) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the external cylindrical area of the barrel nuts [243]. NOTE: Do not apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the self locking feature of the barrel nut. (f) Install the barrel nuts [243] in the holes on the forward mount. 71-00-02 (g) Make sure that the barrel nuts [243] are correctly installed with the retainers at the bottom side. (h) Make sure that the indexing retainer is correctly installed in the indexing recess on the forward mount. SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-004-F00 (10) Do the self-locking check on the four barrel nuts [261] of the aft engine mount (Figure 415). (a) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the bolts [263]. (b) Make sure that the locking torque on the barrel nuts [261] is between 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m). NOTE: Apply only the torque in the above torque range to prevent wear on the barrel nut threads. It is not necessary to find the breakaway torque. (c) If the self-locking torque on the barrel nuts [261] is not between 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m), replace the barrel nuts [261]. (d) Make sure that the retainers do not have cracks or damage. (e) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the external cylindrical area of the barrel nuts [261]. NOTE: Do not apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the self locking feature of the barrel nut. (f) Install the barrel nuts [261] in the holes on the strut. (g) Make sure that the barrel nuts [261] are correctly installed with the retainers on the top side. H. Fan Case Connections on the Left Side

SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-018-F00 (1) Connect the harness connector DP1234 to the strut receptacle (Figure 404). NOTE: All the connections on the left side of the fan case are found at the service disconnect panel on the left side of the fan cowl support beam. SUBTASK 71-00-02-211-001-F00 (2) Do these steps to connect the harness connector D30038 to the strut receptacle (Figure 404). (a) Measure the distance from the end of the connector to the top clamp on the engine. 1) Make sure that the distance is between 13.5 in. (34.3 cm) - 14.0 in. (35.6 cm). 2) If the distance is more than 14.0 in. (35.6 cm), do these steps: a) Loosen the clamps on the engine that hold the integrated drive generator (IDG) power cable and adjust the cable where necessary. b) Make sure that the top clamp is approximately 15 degrees below the horizontal axis. 3) If the distance is correct, install the harness connector D30038 to the strut receptacle. a) If it is necessary, use a crowfoot - 2 9/16 inch, STD-13882. SUBTASK 71-00-02-020-024-F00 (3) If the blanking plate, SPL-18640, is installed, do these steps (View C, Figure 404): (a) Remove the coupling from the starter air duct. (b) Remove the blanking plate, SPL-18640. (c) Remove the E-seal. (d) Examine the duct opening for unwanted material. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-007-F00 (4) Connect the starter duct to the strut as follows: (a) Install the seal [62] on the internal groove of the starter duct. (b) Install the coupling [61] at the top end of the starter duct. 71-00-02 (c) Orient the coupling [61] to give the maximum clearance with the engine and adjacent components. (d) Tighten the coupling [61] to the torque specified on the part. (e) Lightly hit the surface of the coupling [61] with a rubber mallet, STD-3906. (f) Tighten the coupling [61] again to the torque specified on the part. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-008-F00 (5) Connect the hydraulic lines as follows: (a) Remove the protective covers from the hydraulic lines. (b) Connect the quick disconnect couplings on the hydraulic case drain, hydraulic supply and hydraulic pressure lines. 1) Install the hose coupling on the strut fitting. 2) Turn the hose coupling until you can push the hose coupling into the fitting. 3) Turn the hose coupling until the knurled sleeve of the hose coupling snaps on the lock of the fitting. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU FULLY CONNECT THE COUPLING. IF YOU DO NOT , YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE HYDRAULIC PUMP . (c) Make sure that the three quick-release fittings are properly connected both visually and by pulling the outer sleeves away from the male quick-release fittings. 1) Without applying axial force, make sure that the outer sleeves cannot be rotated counterclockwise. NOTE: Without applying axial force, the outer sleeves should only rotate approximately 5 degrees in the clockwise direction. 2) Without turning the outer sleeve, apply axial force to the outer sleeves and make sure that there is little or no movement. 3) If the outer sleeves rotate counterclockwise or pull away from the male quick-release fittings, repeat the steps above to connect the hydraulic hose. NOTE: The quick-release fittings are not properly installed. 4) Make sure that the outer sleeves are fully engaged with the lock tabs on the male quick-release fittings (View D, Figure 404). SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-009-F00 (6) Connect the fuel supply line as follows: (a) Remove the protective covers for the fuel supply line and strut fitting. (b) If it is necessary, loosen the two clamps that attach the fuel supply line to the fan case. NOTE: A loose fuel supply line is easier to install to the strut fitting. CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE HOSE B-NUT . USE ONE TO HOLD THE HOSE, AND THE OTHER TO TIGHTEN THE HOSE B-NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (c) FUEL HOSE WITH A B-NUT FITTING; Do these steps: 1) Use your hand to connect the fuel hose to the strut fitting. 71-00-02 2) Torque the B-nut to 1200 ±60 in-lb (136 ±7 N·m). 3) Loosen the B-nut and re-torque the B-nut to the above torque value. (d) If it is necessary, torque the two clamps that attach the fuel supply line to the fan case. 1) Torque the bolts to 104 ±6 in-lb (12 ±1 N·m). SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-019-F00 (7) Connect the DP0502 connector to the fuel flow transmitter (Figure 409). SUBTASK 71-00-02-220-001-F00 (8) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.15 in. (3.81 mm) between the fire detection wires and the strut insulation blanket. (a) If an adjustment is necessary, refer to this task: Engine Fire Detector Element Installation, TASK 26-11-01-400-801.

SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-001-F00 (25) Make sure that the engine thrust rating shown on the IDENT/CONFIG screen is correct. (a) Get access to the IDENT/CONFIG screen for the other engine and make sure that the engine thrust rating as shown on the screen is the same. (b) Make sure that the Flight Management Computer MEDB Software, thrust reverser configuration, and the opposite engine EEC software are compatible with the new engine (TASK 73-21-60-470-801-F00). NOTE: This step is to make sure that the configuration of the engine to be installed is compatible with the airplane and thrust reversers. This is because EEC software with some part numbers includes a change to the approach idle timer for the thrust reversers. An intermix of one of these software versions and any prior software version currently approved for installation will result in a small difference in idle speeds for three seconds after touchdown if thrust reversers are not deployed. This difference in idle speeds is negligible and requires no change to current flight operations. Thus, the configuration check must be completed in the accordance with the referenced task. 1) Intermix of some EEC software versions is not permitted. 2) Some EEC software versions must be installed on both engines at the same time. 3) Some EEC software versions require concurrent changes to the airplane configuration. (a) You can defer the AAVM memory erasing until the next convenient maintenance opportunity under these conditions: 1) If the AAVM bearing health monitoring features are not being used. No further action required. 2) If the AAVM bearing health monitoring features are being used, then record the date and time of engine change and provide it when submitting data to CFM. RYR ALL SUBTASK 71-00-02-710-001-F00 (29) Do the tests that are listed in the Power Plant Test Reference Table (TASK 71-00-00-800-811-F00). CAUTION DO NOT DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE BEFORE YOU MAKE SURE THAT THE SPAR-VALVE CLOSED LIGHT (ON THE P5 OVERHEAD PANEL) STAYS BRIGHT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE APPLICABLE FOUR LOW PRESSURE LIGHTS ON THE P5 OVERHEAD PANEL ARE OFF . IF YOU DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE AND APPLICABLE LOW PRESSURE LIGHTS ARE ON, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE BEFORE YOU MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS FUEL PRESSURE TO THE FUEL PUMP INLET . THE FUEL PUMP AND HYDRO MECHANICAL UNIT ARE FUEL LUBRICATED. ZERO FUEL PRESSURE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FUEL PUMP AND HYDRO MECHANICAL UNIT . (a) If it is necessary on the engine to be dry motored, apply the boost pump pressure to the fuel pump inlet (Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00). (b) If it is necessary, clear and bleed the applicable pack to prevent cabin odor (oil) after an engine change. 1) Remove the oil contamination from the applicable engine pneumatic ducts (TASK 21-00-01-100-801).
