E. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine F. Power Plant Installation with the Bootstrap Equipment SUBTASK 71-00-02-840-012-F00 (1) Make sure that the power plant is prepared for installation (TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00). SUBTASK 71-00-02-640-007-F00 (2) Lubricate the shear pin [264] on the strut interface of the aft engine mount with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006 (Figure 415). (a) Before you lubricate the shear pin [264], do a visual check of the shear pin for damage. SUBTASK 71-00-02-640-008-F00 (3) Lubricate the two shear pins [242] on the forward engine mount with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006 (Figure 414). (a) Before you lubricate the shear pins [242], do a visual check of the shear pins for damage. SUBTASK 71-00-02-400-001-F00 (4) Do these steps to install the engine mount protector, SPL-23046. NOTE: The engine mount protector, SPL-23046, can be installed between the forward engine mount and the strut to help align the shear pins with the bushings in the strut. This tool is optional. (a) Pull out the handle of the engine mount protector, SPL-23046. NOTE: This will open the shear pin holes in the tool. (b) Align the engine mount protector, SPL-23046, with the strut (insert it from the FWD direction). (c) Install the engine mount protector, SPL-23046, to the strut. (d) Push in the handle of the engine mount protector, SPL-23046. NOTE: This will close the shear pin holes in the tool. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-055-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU VISUALLY INSPECT THE BOOTSTRAP KIT BEFORE USE, INSPECT THE LIFT LUGS FOR GOUGES, LINES, OR CRACKS AT THE LUG ROOT AND THE LANYARD HOLES. IF A LUG JOINT OR STRUCTURE IS SUSPECT , THEN REMOVE IT FROM USE. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT INSTALL TAG LINES ON THE GSE AFT BRACKET . TAG LINES ARE THE ROPES THAT YOU ATTACH TO A LOAD TO CONTROL LOAD SPIN AND PENDULAR MOVEMENT . THIS PREVENTS A SIDE-LOAD THE LIFTING LUGS. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (5) If the bootstrap equipment is not already installed, install the bootstrap kit, SPL-2110, on the strut (Figure 408, Figure 409, Figure 410, Figure 411). 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-037-F00 (6) If the left hand dynamometer assembly [147], right hand dynamometer assembly [151], and dynamometer [183] are attached to the lever hoists [148] and lever hoist [182], remove them temporarily. NOTE: When the dynamometers are removed, you can use the lever hoist hooks as plumb bobs to help align the engine with the strut. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-031-F00 (7) If it is not already done, disconnect the diagonal braces from the left and right forward cradle arms on the dolly. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-038-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU REMOVE THE EYE-BOLTS. IF YOU DO NOT , THE EYE- BOLTS CAN HIT THE FORWARD EDGE OF THE THRUST REVERSER. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (8) AGSE CRADLE; Remove the eye-bolts from the arms of the cradle, COM-2118. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-056-F00 (9) AGSE CRADLE; Put the base, COM-2111, and cradle, COM-2118, with the power plant installed, below the strut as follows (Figure 417): NOTE: When the cradle is in its correct position under the strut, it will not be aligned with the centerline of the strut. (a) Move the dolly/power plant in front of the strut and move it rearward until it is below the strut and the lever hoist hooks are aligned with the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] and engine attach bracket [202]. NOTE: It can be necessary to extend the chains on the lever hoists. NOTE: It is very important to align the cradle with the engine. If they are not aligned, it can be difficult to move the engine from the cradle to the strut. (b) If the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] and engine attach bracket [202] are not aligned with the lever hoist [148] and lever hoist [182], adjust the position of the cradle as follows: 1) Make sure that the castors are not locked. a) If the castors are locked, unlock them. 2) Adjust the position of the cradle. a) Use the cradle steering bars to turn the castors from side to side to adjust the position of the cradle. 3) Visually check if the lever hoist hooks are aligned. a) If the hooks are not aligned, continue to adjust the position of the cradle. b) If the hooks are aligned, lock the wheel castors on the cradle. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-057-F00 (10) F .BROWN CRADLE; Put the engine cradle, COM-4953, and transportation stand, COM-4954, with the power plant installed, below the strut as follows: (a) Move the dolly/power plant in front of the strut and move it aft until it is below the strut and the lever hoist hooks are aligned with the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163]. 1) Make sure that all castors have brakes and steering locks off. 2) When the cradle is aligned, lock the castors. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-058-F00 (11) STANLEY AVIATION CRADLE; Put the engine cradle, COM-6276, and transportation stand, COM-6277, with the power plant installed, below the strut per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-059-F00 (12) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE CRADLE; Put the engine cradle, SPL-14956, and engine trolley, SPL-14957, with the power plant installed, below the strut per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-032-F00 WARNING MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO SPIRAL TWISTS IN THE LEVER HOIST CHAINS BETWEEN THE LEVER HOIST HOUSING AND ITS LOWER BLOCK (THE ATTACH POINT FOR THE DYNAMOMETER). IF YOU SEE A TWIST IN THE CHAIN, YOU MUST REMOVE IT . IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE IT , INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (13) Make sure that the chains on the two lever hoists [148] and lever hoist [182] do not have a spiral twist between the lever hoist housing and lower block (the lower block attaches the chain to the dynamometer). (a) To remove a spiral twist, extend the chain until the twist is removed. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-060-F00 (14) Attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] and right hand dynamometer assembly [151] to the lever hoists [148] (Figure 408). NOTE: The two dynamometers must face forward. To do this, the left dynamometer must be installed upside down. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-061-F00 (15) Attach the dynamometer [183] to the lever hoist [182] (Figure 410). SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-062-F00 (16) Attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] and right lower link assembly [150] to the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] with the lockpins [161] (Figure 409). (a) If it is necessary, adjust the length of the two lever hoists [148]. (b) Attach the safety pin to the end of each lockpin [161]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-480-063-F00 (17) Attach the aft dynamometer [183] to the engine attach bracket [202] with a lockpin [201] (Figure 411). NOTE: If it is necessary, adjust the length of the lever hoist [182]. (a) Attach the safety pin to the end of each lockpin [201]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-033-F00 (18) Make sure that the forward and aft bootstrap and all engine attach brackets are installed correctly. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-034-F00 (19) Before you apply a load to the bootstrap equipment, make sure that all dynamometers are set to the zero position. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-039-F00 CAUTION ONE PERSON MUST MONITOR EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN YOU OPERATE THE LEVER HOISTS. WHEN YOU CHANGE THE LOADS AT ONE HOIST , THE LOADS CAN CHANGE AT OTHER HOISTS. THIS CAN CAUSE LOADS THAT ARE HIGHER THAN THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (20) AGSE CRADLE; Disconnect the engine from the cradle, COM-2118, as follows (Figure 412): CAUTION DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 3850 LB (1746 KG) TO THE FORWARD INBOARD DYNAMOMETER, AND 3350 LB (1520 KG) TO THE FORWARD OUTBOARD DYNAMOMETER. IF YOU APPLY MORE THAN THE LIMITS, DAMAGE TO THE POWER PLANT , WING, AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. (a) Use the forward lever hoists [148] and aft lever hoist [182] to slowly lift the weight of the engine from the cradle. (b) Use the aft lever hoist [182] and adjust the load to disconnect the aft support arm from the Turbine Rear Frame (TRF). 1) Remove the lockpin [281] and move the support arm to rest on the cradle. (c) Disconnect the forward cradle arms from the engine: 1) Disengage the spanner nut on the right trunnion. a) Thread the nut inboard almost to the end of the threaded shaft. 2) If it is necessary, use the forward lever hoist [148] and adjust the load to remove the lockpin [221] from each trunnion. 3) Slide the trunnions away from the engine until stopped by the capscrews. a) Make sure that the end support balls are clear of the engine-to-cradle attach bracket [163]. 4) Remove the lower lockpins from each forward cradle arm and turn the arms to the outboard position. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-036-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU LIFT THE LOAD EQUALLY . MAKE SURE THAT LIFT CABLES ARE VERTICAL. ONE PERSON MUST MONITOR EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN YOU OPERATE THE LEVER HOISTS. WHEN YOU CHANGE THE LOADS AT ONE HOIST , THE LOADS CAN CHANGE AT OTHER HOISTS. THIS CAN CAUSE LOADS THAT ARE HIGHER THAN THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (21) F .BROWN CRADLE; Disconnect the engine from the engine cradle, COM-4953, as follows (Figure 413): CAUTION DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 3850 LB (1746 KG) TO THE FORWARD INBOARD DYNAMOMETER, AND 3350 LB (1520 KG) TO THE FORWARD OUTBOARD DYNAMOMETER. IF YOU APPLY MORE THAN THE LIMITS, DAMAGE TO THE POWER PLANT , WING, AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. (a) Use the forward lever hoists [148] and aft lever hoist [182] to slowly lift the weight of the engine from the cradle. (b) Release the forward clamp assemblies. 71-00-02 1) Loosen the collar nuts. 2) Move the swing bolts to the unlock position. 3) Open the clamp assemblies. (c) Use the aft lever hoist [182] and adjust the load to disconnect the aft support arm from the TRF . 1) Remove the lockpin and move the support arm to rest on the cradle. (d) Remove the forward trunnions from the engine: 1) Continue to lift the engine until the trunnions become loose in their cradle clamp sockets. 2) Remove the trunnions from the engine and store them safely to one side. (e) Put the forward clamp assemblies to the stowed position: 1) Close the clamp assembly. 2) Put the swing bolts in the lock position and tighten the collar nuts. 3) Remove the hinge pin and put the clamp assembly to the stowed position. 4) Install the hinge pin and safety pin. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-037-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU LIFT THE LOAD EQUALLY . MAKE SURE THAT LIFT CABLES ARE VERTICAL. ONE PERSON MUST MONITOR EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN YOU OPERATE THE LEVER HOISTS. WHEN YOU CHANGE THE LOADS AT ONE HOIST , THE LOADS CAN CHANGE AT OTHER HOISTS. THIS CAN CAUSE LOADS THAT ARE HIGHER THAN THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (22) STANLEY AVIATION CRADLE; Disconnect the engine from the engine cradle, COM-6276, per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-038-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU LIFT THE LOAD EQUALLY . MAKE SURE THAT LIFT CABLES ARE VERTICAL. ONE PERSON MUST MONITOR EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN YOU OPERATE THE LEVER HOISTS. WHEN YOU CHANGE THE LOADS AT ONE HOIST , THE LOADS CAN CHANGE AT OTHER HOISTS. THIS CAN CAUSE LOADS THAT ARE HIGHER THAN THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (23) DEDIENNE AEROSPACE CRADLE; Disconnect the engine from the engine cradle, SPL-14956, per the vendor manual. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-035-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU LIFT THE LOAD EQUALLY . MAKE SURE THAT LIFT CABLES ARE VERTICAL. ONE PERSON MUST MONITOR EACH DYNAMOMETER WHEN YOU OPERATE THE LEVER HOISTS. WHEN YOU CHANGE THE LOADS AT ONE HOIST , THE LOADS CAN CHANGE AT OTHER HOISTS. THIS CAN CAUSE LOADS THAT ARE HIGHER THAN THE MAXIMUM BOOTSTRAP LOADS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (24) Slowly increase the load on the left hand dynamometer assembly [147], right hand dynamometer assembly [151], and dynamometer [183] to raise the engine. (a) Make sure that you observe these areas: 71-00-02 1) The forward side of the fan cowl support beam and aft side of the inlet cowl at the 12:00 location. 2) The fire extinguishing tube and precooler inlet duct flange. 3) The forward side of the thrust reversers and aft side of the fan case at the 12:00 position. 4) The top of the exhaust nozzle and bottom of the strut fairing. 5) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG; The interference pin at the 12:00 o'clock position on the exhaust nozzle shelf and mating receptacle in the strut. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-036-F00 (25) Use the forward outboard lever hoist [148] to roll the engine until it is parallel to the engine mounts on the strut (approximately 6 degrees). SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-037-F00 (26) As you continue to raise the engine, raise the aft end slightly higher than the forward end. NOTE: This will keep the above interference areas to a minimum. NOTE: The forward mount can move in a forward and aft direction. Make sure that the forward mount remains free as you engage the forward shear pins [242]. (a) If the forward mount binds, lower the engine until the shear pins [242] are free. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-038-F00 (27) As you engage the shear pin [242] and shear pin [264], make sure that the engine mount surfaces are parallel with the strut. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-039-F00 (28) If the engine mount protector, SPL-23046, was used, do these steps to remove the engine mount protector, SPL-23046: (a) Pull out the handle on engine mount protector, SPL-23046. NOTE: This will open the shear pin holes in the tool. (b) Remove the engine mount protector, SPL-23046, from the strut. SUBTASK 71-00-02-970-002-F00 (29) Record the applied engine load from left hand dynamometer assembly [147], right hand dynamometer assembly [151], and dynamometer [183]. NOTE: This data will be used when the preload is applied later. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-040-F00 (30) Continue to raise the engine until the engine mounts are 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) - 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) below the strut. (a) Make sure that the aft mount surfaces are parallel to the mating strut surface. (b) If they are not, use the forward lever hoist [148] to adjust the alignment of the aft mount. (c) When you get the correct alignment, use the aft lever hoist [182] to raise the aft mount against the mating strut surface. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-021-F00 (31) If the rear shear pin [264] does not fully engage and clearance of approximately 0.3 in. (7.6 mm), make sure that the exhaust nozzle is compatible with the strut (Figure 418). NOTE: The short exhaust nozzle has an interference pin at the 12 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf. To use this nozzle, there must be a mating receptacle in the strut. If this receptacle is not found, the strut is not compatible with the exhaust nozzle. You must install the long exhaust nozzle and long exhaust plug on this engine. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-041-F00 (32) Slowly raise the two forward lever hoists [148] equally until the forward mount is engaged with the mating strut surfaces. SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-022-F00 (33) Examine the strut fireseal to make sure that it is seated correctly and does not protrude over the engine fan case. (a) Use a plastic spatula at each corner of the seal to push the last horizontal section (3.0 in. (76.2 mm) - 4.0 in. (101.6 mm) long) of the seal forward over the edge of the fan case coaming. 1) This step prevents the protrusion of the fireseal corners into the bypass duct after the thrust reverser is closed. (b) To examine the forward strut fireseal, do this task: Forward Strut Fireseal Inspection, TASK 54-54-00-200-802. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-042-F00 (34) Apply a preload to the lever hoists [148] and lever hoist [182] as follows: CAUTION DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 3850 POUNDS (1746 KG) TO THE FORWARD INBOARD DYNAMOMETER, 3350 POUNDS (1520 KG) TO THE FORWARD OUTBOARD DYNAMOMETER AND 1300 POUNDS (590 KG) TO THE AFT DYNAMOMETER. IF YOU APPLY MORE THAN THE LIMITS, DAMAGE TO THE POWER PLANT , WING AND STRUT CAN OCCUR. (a) Apply loads to the left hand dynamometer assembly [147], right hand dynamometer assembly [151], and dynamometer [183] that are more than the applied engine load values that you recorded earlier. NOTE: There is no specific load value that must be applied. The only limits are that the loads must be more than the applied engine load values and that the strut mating surfaces and the engine mounts stay together. SUBTASK 71-00-02-820-043-F00 (35) If after the preload is applied there is a clearance between the forward or aft mounts, remove the clearance as follows: (a) Use a Feeler Gauge, STD-5468, and insert the 0.0030 ±0.0005 in. (0.0762 ±0.0127 mm) feeler gauge between the strut mating surfaces and engine mounts. 1) If the feeler gauge does not contact the shear pins, the clearance/gap is acceptable. 2) If the feeler gauge does contact the shear pins, do these steps: (b) If there is a clearance in the aft mount, first shake the aft mount. 71-00-02 1) If the clearance remains, use the applicable forward lever hoist [148] to roll the engine to the side with the clearance. NOTE: As an example, if the clearance is on the inboard side, decrease the load on the outboard forward lever hoist [148] to roll the engine to the inboard position. (c) If there is a clearance in the forward mount, first shake the forward mount. 1) If the clearance remains, use the applicable forward lever hoist [148] to roll the engine to the side with the clearance. NOTE: As an example, if the clearance is on the inboard side, decrease the load on the outboard forward lever hoist [148] to roll the engine to the inboard position. SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-023-F00 (36) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG; Make sure that the interference pin at the 12:00 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf is centered in the mating receptacle on the strut (Figure 418). NOTE: The short exhaust nozzle has an interference pin at the 12 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf, To use this nozzle, there must be a mating receptacle in the strut. If this receptacle is not found, the strut is not compatible with the exhaust nozzle. You must install the long exhaust nozzle and long exhaust plug on this engine. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-039-F00 (37) Attach the power plant to the strut as follows: NOTE: Before you tighten the eight bolts that attach the power plant to the strut, you must do a check of the self-locking feature on the forward and aft barrel nuts. If not already done, refer to the procedure, Prepare For The Power Plant Installation. (a) Loosely install the forward engine mount to the strut (Figure 414): 1) Put a washer [244] on each bolt [241]. 2) Make sure that the countersunk side of the washer [244] is adjacent to the head of the bolt [241]. 3) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads and shank of the bolts [241]. 4) Install the four bolts [241] and four washers [244] in the forward engine mount. (b) Install the bolts [241], but do not tighten the bolts [241]. (c) Loosely install the aft engine mount to the strut (Figure 415): 1) Install a washer [262] on each bolt [263]. 2) Make sure that the countersunk side of the washer [262] is adjacent to the head of the bolt [263]. 3) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads and shank of the bolts [263]. 4) Install the four bolts [263] and four washers [262] in the aft engine mount. (d) Install the bolts [263], but do not tighten the bolts [263]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-040-F00 (38) Apply the initial torque with wrench, SPL-2106, as follows: (a) Cross-tighten the forward engine mount bolts [241] to 45 ft-lb (61.0 N·m) - 55 ft-lb (74.6 N·m). 71-00-02 (b) Cross-tighten the aft engine mount bolts [263] to 80 ft-lb (108.5 N·m) - 98 ft-lb (132.9 N·m). SUBTASK 71-00-02-420-041-F00 (39) Apply the final torque as follows: (a) Tighten the forward engine mount bolts [241] to 90 ft-lb (122.0 N·m) - 110 ft-lb (149.1 N·m). 1) Make sure that the mating connection of the forward mount bolts [241] is free of oil, grease, and other unwanted material (SOPM 20-30-03). 2) Apply tamper-proof putty/lacquer, G51905, to the mating connection of the bolts [241]. (b) Tighten the aft engine mount bolts [263] to 160 ft-lb (216.9 N·m) - 195 ft-lb (264.4 N·m). 1) Make sure that the mating connection of the aft mount bolts [263] is free of oil, grease, and other unwanted material (SOPM 20-30-03). 2) Apply tamper-proof putty/lacquer, G51905, to the mating connection of the bolts [263]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-040-F00 (40) Remove the dolly from the work area. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-041-F00 (41) Remove the load from the lever hoists [148] and lever hoist [182]. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-042-F00 (42) Disconnect the bootstrap equipment from the power plant as follows: (a) Disconnect the forward bootstrap equipment (Figure 409): 1) Disconnect the lockpins [161] that attach the left hand dynamometer assembly [147] and right lower link assembly [150] to the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163]. 2) Remove the bolts [162] that attach the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163] to the fan case. 3) Remove the cradle-to-engine attach brackets [163]. (b) Disconnect the aft bootstrap equipment (Figure 411): 1) Disconnect the lockpin [201] that attaches the aft dynamometer [183] to the engine attach bracket [202]. 2) Disconnect the two lockpins [203] that attach the aft engine attach bracket [202] to the engine flange bracket [204] and engine flange bracket [205]. 3) Remove the engine attach bracket [202]. (c) Put all removed brackets in the storage box on the cradle. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-043-F00 (43) Remove the forward bootstrap equipment from the strut as follows (Figure 408): (a) Remove the right hand dynamometer assembly [151] and left hand lever hoist [148] from forward arms. (b) Release the brace [142] from the inboard arm [143] as follows: NOTE: There are two braces on the forward bootstrap. They consist of a metal rod with a clevis on one end and permanently attached lockpin at the other end. 1) Disconnect the lockpin [149] that attaches the clevis on the forward end of the brace [142] to the strut. 71-00-02 2) Turn the brace [142] 90 degrees until the brace lockpin is aligned with the keyed slot in the inboard arm [143]. 3) Move the brace [142] forward until it is disengaged from the inboard arm [143]. (c) Do the above step again to release the other brace [142]. (d) Disconnect the lockpin [144] that attaches the outboard arm [145] to the inboard arm [143] at the top location. NOTE: Each arm has a shear pin below the strut attach fitting to temporarily hold the arm in its installed position. The arms will not fall. (e) To remove the outboard arm [145], disconnect the lockpin [146] at the strut attach fitting. (f) To remove the inboard arm [143], disconnect the lockpin [141] at the strut attach fitting. SUBTASK 71-00-02-410-007-F00 (44) For the thumbnail fairing, do this task: Forward Fairing Installation, TASK 54-52-01-410-801. SUBTASK 71-00-02-080-044-F00 (45) Remove the aft bootstrap equipment from the strut as follows (Figure 410): (a) Disconnect the lockpin [189] and remove the dynamometer [183] and lever hoist [182] from the support beam [184]. (b) To disconnect the support beam [184], hold it as you disconnect the outboard lockpin assembly [187]. 1) Slide the support beam [184] out until it is free of the aft support brace [186] and forward support brace [188]. (c) Remove the lockpin assembly [185] that attaches the aft support brace [186] and forward support brace [188] together at the inboard location. (d) Remove the forward support brace [188]. (e) Remove the aft support brace [186]. NOTE: The strut attach brackets are permanently attached to the strut and are not removed. (0.0762 ±0.0127 mm) feeler gauge between the strut mating surfaces and engine mounts. 1) If the feeler gauge does not contact the shear pins, the clearance/gap is acceptable. 2) If the feeler gauge does contact the shear pins, do these steps: a) If there is a clearance in the aft mount, first shake the aft mount. <1> If the clearance remains, operate the JACXSON U70 to slightly lower and readjust the engine. b) If there is a clearance in the forward mount, first shake the forward mount. <1> If the clearance remains, operate the JACXSON U70 to slightly lower and readjust the engine. 71-00-02 SUBTASK 71-00-02-210-025-F00 (17) ENGINES WITH THE SHORT EXHAUST NOZZLE AND SHORT EXHAUST PLUG; Make sure that the interference pin at the 12:00 o'clock position on the nozzle shelf is centered in the mating receptacle on the strut (Figure 418). ATA 71 · 71-00-03

17 tasks
71-00-03-600-801-F00Dry-Out and Lubrication of the Engine ATA 71 · Task 600-801-F00

Task Description

2. Dry-Out and Lubrication of the Engine (Figure 201, Figure 202, Figure 203, Figure 204)

A. General

(1) This task is to dry the forward sump, aft sump, and the gearbox of the engine with hot air when the engine can not be operated. WARNING DO THE DRY-OUT PROCEDURE IN AN AREA WITH A GOOD AIRFLOW. KEEP CLEAR OF THE ENGINE EXHAUST AREA. DO NOT BREATHE THE OIL MIST FROM THE ENGINE EXHAUST . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE PRECAUTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR CAUTION IF AN IN-FLIGHT SHUTDOWN OCCURRED ON THE APPLICABLE ENGINE AND THE ENGINE WILL NOT BE OPERATED FOR 24 HOURS AFTER A LANDING, YOU MUST DO THE ENGINE DRY-OUT PROCEDURE AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE. IF YOU DO NOT DO THE ENGINE DRY-OUT PROCEDURE IMMEDIATELY AFTER A LANDING, CONDENSATION CAN CAUSE CORROSION DAMAGE ON THE COMPONENTS WET WITH OIL. (2) This task gives the dry-out and lubrication steps that are necessary for the engine that had an in-flight shutdown. NOTE: You must do this procedure not longer than 24 hours after landing. (3) If the engine is to be operated in the 24 hours after it landed, run the engine for a minimum of 20 minutes at low idle. (4) If the engine run is performed in the 24 hours after landing, it is not necessary to do the Dry-Out and Lubrication of the Engine. In this case, run the engine for a minimum of 20 minutes at low idle.

Prepare for the Dry-Out and Lubrication Procedure SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-001-F00 (1) For engines that are removed from the airplane, use the CFM Engine Shop Manual, Section 72-00-00, page 1201. SUBTASK 71-00-03-040-001-F00 (2) For engines that are installed on the wing of the airplane, do these steps: (a) Install a DO-NOT-OPERATE tag on the applicable start switch. (b) Install the sealing plate from the Locking Adapter, SPL-11931 with its bolts [1]. (c) Tighten the bolts to 101 ±5 in-lb (11 ±1 N·m). SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-002-F00 (6) Prepare the re-lubrication manifold from tool set, SPL-2448 as follows (Figure 202): (a) Remove the protective covers from the relubrication manifold openings. (b) Remove the knurled protectors from the pushers. (c) Examine the O-rings on the pushers. 1) Replace the O-rings if you find damage. (d) Remove the knurled bolts from the relubrication manifold. IF YOU APPLY FORCE TO THE PUSHER, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (g) Carefully install one of the pushers (with locking pins) into the aft sump hole of the lubrication unit housing. 1) Align the pusher keys with the lubrication unit sleeve keyways. 2) Push until the pusher is fully in the hole. 3) Turn the pusher one quarter of a turn clockwise to engage in the keyways. (h) Make sure the pusher is in its locked position: 1) Pull the pusher down. 2) Lightly turn the pusher from side to side to make sure the pusher is 'snapped' down. (i) Set the plate (from aft side) into the groove of the pusher. (j) Move the plate forward to engage the pusher. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY FORCE TO THE PUSHER TO INSTALL IT INTO THE LUBRICATION UNIT . IF YOU APPLY FORCE TO THE PUSHER, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (k) Carefully install one of the pushers (without locking pins) into the forward sump hole of the lubrication unit housing. 1) Push until the pusher is fully in the hole. (l) Hold the pusher tightly with one hand. (m) Push the plate forward with your other hand until it move into the pusher groove. 71-00-03 CAUTION DO NOT APPLY FORCE TO THE PUSHER TO INSTALL IT INTO THE LUBRICATION UNIT . IF YOU APPLY FORCE TO THE PUSHER, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (n) Carefully install the last pusher (with locking pins) into the TGB/AGB hole of the lubrication unit housing: 1) Align the pusher keys with the lubrication unit sleeve keyways. 2) Push until the pusher is fully in the hole. 3) Turn the pusher one quarter of a turn clockwise to engage the key in the keyways. (o) Make sure the pusher is in its locked position: 1) Pull the pusher down. 2) Lightly turn the pusher from side to side. NOTE: This is to make sure the pusher is 'snapped' down. (p) Push the plate forward into the groove of the last pusher. 1) Make sure the plate fully engages all three pushers. (q) Remove the protective covers from the air filter openings. (r) Install the relubrication manifold on the three pushers with the air supply connector pointed aft. (s) Attach the manifold to the plate with the 4 knurled bolts. 1) Use your hand to tighten the bolts. (t) Make sure the manifold is fully against the plate. (u) Fill the oil container of the relubrication tool set with one of these solutions: 1) Use 1.7 pints (800 ml) of additive, D00662 [CP5075]. 2) To make the alternate oil solution, do these steps: a) Use 0.85 pints (400 ml) of anti-corrosion additive (CP2309). b) Use 0.85 pints (400 ml) of oil, D00599 [CP2442]. (v) Connect the air pressure supply line to the nipple of the oil container. (w) Connect the oil supply line to the nipple of the oil container. (x) Make sure the oil supply valve is closed.

G. The Power Plant Dry-Out Procedure

SUBTASK 71-00-03-600-001-F00 (1) Do the power plant dry-out procedure as follows (Figure 203): (a) Use the adapter, SPL-2251 to examine the air filter for unwanted material. 1) Blow dry, filtered, compressed air through hoses to remove all unwanted material. (b) Do these steps to install the air adapter, SPL-2253 on the engine exhaust plug: 1) Install the half flanges on the engine exhaust plug. 2) Tighten the screw to 447.5 ±22.5 in-lb (50.6 ±2.5 N·m). 3) Put the tubing at the end of exhaust plug. 4) Attach the tubing to the half flanges with the four threaded rods. 5) Tighten the four nuts. 71-00-03 (c) Do these steps to install the first hose of the adapter, SPL-2251 to the hot air source: 1) Install one end to the hot air supply outlet. 2) Install the other end to the air filter inlet. 3) Attach each hose end with a clamp. (d) Do these steps to install the second hose of the adapter, SPL-2251 to the air adapter, SPL-2253: 1) Install one end to the air filter outlet. 2) Install the other end to the air adapter, SPL-2253. 3) Attach each hose end with a clamp. (e) Install the protective mat, STD-585 in the inlet on the full lower half of the inlet cowl. WARNING STAY CLEAR OF THE RELUBRICATION MANIFOLD INSTALLED ON THE LUBRICATION UNIT BY A MINIMUM OF 20 FEET (6 METERS). THE RELUBRICATION MANIFOLD BLOWS HOT AIR AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. (f) Turn ON the hot air source. 1) Let the pressure increase slowly to the operation level. 2) The air temperature must be 300-325 degrees F (150-165 degrees C). (g) Do the dry-out cycle for a minimum of 20 minutes. WARNING DO NOT MANUALLY TURN THE FAN ROTOR WITHOUT GOOD GLOVES. MAKE SURE YOU ARE ON A SAFE SURFACE WHILE YOU TURN THE FAN. BE VERY CAREFUL WHILE YOU TURN THE FAN TO PREVENT INJURY . 1) Use insulated gloves, STD-1085 to turn the fan rotor slowly in a counterclockwise direction. NOTE: One full turn in the usual operational direction. 2) Turn the fan rotor slowly one full turn every five minutes for 20 minutes. (h) Turn OFF the hot air source when you complete the cycle time. (i) Remove the hot air source hose from the adapter, SPL-2251. (j) Remove the air adapter, SPL-2253 from the engine exhaust plug.

H. The Lubrication Procedure

SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-003-F00 (1) Do the lubrication procedure as follows (Figure 204): (a) Move the hot air source hose to the air supply connector of the relubrication manifold. 1) Attach the hose end with a clamp. (b) Turn ON the hot air source. 1) Let the pressure increase slowly to the operation level. 2) The air temperature must be 300-325 degrees F (150-165 degrees C). 71-00-03 WARNING STAY CLEAR OF THE ENGINE EXHAUST AREA. IF YOU BREATHE THE OIL MIST FROM THE ENGINE EXHAUST , INJURY CAN OCCUR. (c) Open the oil supply valve when you see hot air move from the engine exhaust. WARNING DO NOT MANUALLY TURN THE FAN ROTOR WITHOUT GOOD GLOVES. MAKE SURE YOU ARE ON A SAFE SURFACE WHILE YOU TURN THE FAN. BE VERY CAREFUL WHILE YOU TURN THE FAN TO PREVENT INJURY . (d) Use insulated gloves, STD-1085 to turn the fan rotor slowly in a counterclockwise direction. NOTE: One full turn in the usual operational direction. (e) Turn the N2 rotor slowly one full turn each minute. (f) Move the fan rotor until the oil container is empty. NOTE: This usually takes five to six minutes. (g) Do these steps when the oil container is empty: 1) Close the oil supply valve. 2) Shut OFF the hot air source.

I. The Dry-Out and Lubrication Equipment Removal

SUBTASK 71-00-03-080-001-F00 (1) Do these steps to remove the Dry-Out and Lubrication Equipment (Figure 201, Figure 202). (a) Remove the hot air source hose from the relubrication manifold and the air filter outlet. (b) Remove the hose from the air filter inlet and the hot air source. (c) Remove the oil supply line from the oil container. (d) Remove the air pressure supply line from the oil container. (e) Do these steps to remove the relubrication manifold and plate: 1) Remove the four knurled bolts 2) Remove the relubrication manifold. 3) Remove the forward sump pusher while you move the plate: a) Push the pusher in and turn one quarter turn counterclockwise to release the locking keys. 4) Do these steps to remove the aft sump pusher and the TGB/AGB pusher. a) Push each pusher in and turn one quarter turn counterclockwise to release the locking keys. 5) Install protective covers on the relubrication manifold openings. (f) Examine the air filter for unwanted material. (g) Clean the air filter if there is unwanted material on it. (h) Install protective covers on the air filter openings. SUBTASK 71-00-03-410-001-F00 (2) Do this task: Magnetic Chip Detector (MCD) Installation, TASK 79-21-05-400-804-F00 or Debris Monitoring System (DMS) Detector Installation, TASK 79-21-05-400-805-F00. 71-00-03 RYR ALL; FOR ALL NON 7BE PRE CFM SB 72-0564 OR PRE SB 72-0879 SUBTASK 71-00-03-080-002-F00 (3) Remove the core engine sealing plate as follows: (a) Remove the bolts [1]. (b) Remove the plate. SUBTASK 71-00-03-410-002-F00 (4) Do this task: Handcranking Drive Cover Installation, TASK 72-63-01-400-801-F00. RYR ALL

J. Put the Engine Back to its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 71-00-03-840-001-F00 (1) Do these steps: (a) Remove the protective mat, STD-585 from the inlet cowl. (b) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00. (c) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag on the applicable start switch. (d) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag from the engine start lever.

71-00-03-600-815-F00Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure ATA 71 · Task 600-815-F00

Task Description

3. Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure (Figure 205)

A. General

(1) This task provides instructions to apply a protective coating on the inlet cowl lipskin to prevent corrosion. NOTE: It is acceptable to leave the inlet cowl lipskin bare if the engine is preserved for 7 days or less. NOTE: It is recommended checking the lipskins for visual appearance every two weeks for the first two months and reapplying protective coating as necessary. Operators can then adjust their schedule based on operational environment and use of the aircraft. RYR ALL POST SB 737-71-1717 NOTE: This procedure is not applicable if heat resistant aluminized paint (HRAP) has been applied to the inlet lip skin. If HRAP has been applied, no additional corrosion protections are required on the lip skin. RYR ALL (2) The task includes the procedure to remove the protective coating. (3) This task should be done if the engine (on-wing) is preserved for more than 7 days. (4) There are three methods to preserve the inlet cowl lipskin: (a) Method 1 - Apply the corrosion preventative compound X20-18 compound, G51625, to the lipskin. NOTE: The X20-18 compound, G51625, can be left on the lipskin during engine idle runs if the engine anti-ice system is deactivated. NOTE: If the engine anti-ice system is to be turned on during engine idle runs, the X20-18 compound, G51625, coating must be removed and reapplied after the engine run. NOTE: The X20-18 compound, G51625, coating must be removed prior to return to service. NOTE: Please refer to the supplier instructions for additional information regarding the application and removal of X20-18 compound, G51625. (b) Method 2 - Apply the peelable protective coating system, Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013/Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, PPG Z6160 coating, C50411/PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, or Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410. NOTE: Boeing recommends that peelable protective coatings be applied to the inlet lipskin when airplanes are stored indoors or when using a typical inlet cover that covers the inlet lipskin and nacelles. NOTE: The consumable materials Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013, and Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, are now discontinued by the manufacturer. The coatings can still be used as a coating system and operators are encouraged to use any existing stock before using the alternative materials PPG Z6160 coating, C50411/PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, or Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410. NOTE: Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013/Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, PPG Z6160 coating, C50411/PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, or Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, must be removed prior to engine runs. 71-00-03 (c) Method 3 - Weekly inspection for corrosion and cleaning.

B. References

Reference Title 20-10-34-110-802 Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent (P/B 701) 30-00-00-040-803 MMEL 30-03 (DDPG) Preparation - Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valves Inoperative (P/B 901) 30-00-00-440-803 MMEL 30-03 (DDPG) Restoration - Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valves Inoperative (P/B 901) SOPM 20-30-03 General Cleaning Procedures

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1064 Scraper - Phenolic, Hard Resin

D. Consumable Materials

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine 71-00-03 F. Method 1 - Protective Coating Application WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU READ THE MANUFACTURER'S SAFETY DATA SHEET (MSDS) FOR THE MATERIALS YOU WILL USE, AND WEAR THE PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT IF IT IS SPECIFIED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-002-F00 (1) If it is necessary, remove existing pitting, corrosion and surface oxidation from the inlet cowl lipskin. (a) Use the applicable Structural Repair Manual (SRM) procedure. (b) Make sure that the minimum thickness requirements per the SRM are met. SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-003-F00 (2) Prepare the lipskin for the application of X20-18 compound, G51625. (a) Clean the lipskin with XS3 Aircraft Wash and XG5 Hard Surface Cleaner furnished from the X20-18 compound, G51625, vendor prior to application. NOTE: X20-18 compound, G51625, will not remove corrosion but will act to assist in preventing future corrosion. It is acceptable to perform general solvent cleaning per Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802 as an alternative to the products recommended by Grantize. (b) Remove any dust, dirt, unwanted material, oil, grease or moisture. SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-005-F00 (3) Mask the lipskin. (a) Mask the inner and outer barrel assembly and the fan compartment. (b) Make sure that the sealant common to the lipskin is protected. (c) It is permitted for about 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) of the lipskin to be unprotected. (d) Apply Rulon J tape, G02356, to the three radial seams of the lipskin. (e) Do not apply the protective coating to the acoustic barrel area. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-005-F00 (4) Prepare for the application of X20-18 compound, G51625, to the lipskin. (a) Make sure that the lipskin surface temperature is between 67.5 ±22.5°F (19.7 ±12.5°C). (b) Avoid application of X20-18 compound, G51625, when the ambient humidity is above 90%. (c) Apply a few drops of the X20-18 compound, G51625, to a soft cotton applicator. Do not saturate the applicator to the point of dripping. NOTE: If the X20-18 compound, G51625, pours out in a cloudy or milky consistency, do not use it. Discard the remaining contents. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-006-F00 (5) Apply X20-18 compound, G51625, to the lipskin. (a) Apply a thin film of X20-18 compound, G51625, to an area of 2.5 ±0.5 ft 2 (0.2 ±0.0 m 2) in a sweeping motion. 71-00-03 1) Do not allow the X20-18 compound, G51625, to dry. Wipe the treated area immediately with a dry and soft cloth until all wet film is buffed off and no longer visible. Rotate the cloth as necessary when absorbency decreases. NOTE: The initial application of the X20-18 compound, G51625, may remove remaining amounts of polishing residue if cleaning wasn't completed adequately. If only a small amount; proceed with application. Otherwise, repeat cleaning steps in previous section. NOTE: Direct exposure to sunlight or warm surface temperatures can result in streaking. (b) Repeat application process until entire lipskin is treated. The process is complete when three (3) coats are applied. NOTE: The process is complete when three coats are applied. 1) Allow a minimum of 30 minutes between coat applications. NOTE: X20-18 compound, G51625, has a 12 hour cure time. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-007-F00 (6) It is recommended to repolish and reapply X20-18 compound, G51625, at a cycle of every ninety (90) days or after the surface loses its shine. Whichever occurs first. NOTE: Boeing recommends a schedule for checking the lipskin visual appearance every two (2) weeks for the first two (2) months and then adjusting the schedule according to operator experience based on environment and use of airplane. (a) To detect the presence of X20-18 compound, G51625, on bare metal surfaces, perform one of the following: 1) Use Rulon J tape, G02356, fold one end back to make a tab at the end. Firmly press the tape on a subject treated area and suspected untreated area. Pull the tab back slowly at a 90 degree angle to the surface. Noticeable ease in resistance will take place on a treated surface compared to a non-treated surface. 2) Spray clean deionized water on the surface. Moisture will bead up on a treated surface when compared to a non-treated surface. SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-006-F00 (7) Remove the masking material from the inner and outer barrels and the fan compartment. SUBTASK 71-00-03-040-002-F00 (8) If engine idle runs will be performed throughout aircraft storage, it is required to deactivate the engine anti-ice system if X20-18 compound, G51625, is still applied to the lipskin. Deactivating the engine anti-ice system will allow the X20-18 compound, G51625, to be left on during engine runs. NOTE: Failure to keep the Engine Anti Ice deactivated during the entire engine run with AECI 3 applied to the lipskin would cause AECI 3 burning, and will result in permanent staining of the lipskin. (a) Make sure that the X20-18 compound, G51625, has cured for 12 hours before performing engine runs. (b) Deactivate the engine anti-ice system with the engine anti-ice valve inoperative CLOSED (TASK 30-00-00-040-803). NOTE: The system can be left deactivated throughout storage. There is no need to do the restoration procedure after each engine run. 71-00-03

G. Method 2 - Protective Coating Application

WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU READ THE MANUFACTURER'S SAFETY DATA SHEET (MSDS) FOR THE MATERIALS YOU WILL USE, AND WEAR THE PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT IF IT IS SPECIFIED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-005-F00 (1) If it is necessary, remove existing pitting, corrosion and surface oxidation from inlet cowl lipskin. (a) Use the applicable SRM procedure. (b) Make sure that the minimum thickness requirements per the SRM are met. SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-001-F00 (2) Clean the lipskin and get a water break free surface. (a) Use a lint-free cloth, G00834, and solvent, B00666, to wipe the lipskin. (b) Remove any dust, dirt, unwanted material, oil, grease or moisture. SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-003-F00 (3) Mask the lipskin. (a) Mask the inner and outer barrel assembly and the fan compartment. (b) Make sure that the sealant common to the lipskin is protected. (c) It is permitted for about 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) of the lipskin to be unprotected. (d) Apply Rulon J tape, G02356, to the three radial seams of the lipskin. (e) Do not apply the protective coating to the acoustic barrel area. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-001-F00 (4) Prepare the basecoat Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013. (a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.1°C) - 80°F (26.7°C). (b) Mix the material to a homogeneous consistency. (c) Standard spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and pot pressure of 5 psi (34.5 kPa) is recommended to get the proper fluid delivery. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-002-F00 (5) Apply the basecoat Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013, to the lipskin. (a) Apply a 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment. (b) Let this layer dry for 1 hour. NOTE: You can decrease this time with warm air or infrared lamps. Protect the area from freezing. (c) Apply a second layer to get a total of 8 mils (0.008 in.) thickness. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-003-F00 (6) Prepare the Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014. (a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.1°C) - 80°F (26.7°C). (b) Mix the material to a homogeneous consistency. (c) Apply the topcoat in two separate layers using standard spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and pot pressure of 5 psi (34.5 kPa). 71-00-03 SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-004-F00 (7) Apply the Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, to the lipskin. (a) Make sure that the basecoat is dry (no gloss). (b) The temperature at the time of application and drying should be a minimum of 40°F (4.4°C). Protect the area from freezing. (c) Dry apply the first layer of topcoat over the basecoat with a wide fan and the gun held about 18 in. (45.7 cm) from the surface. 1) This discontinuous layer should barely cover the black basecoat to minimize bubbles in the protective coating. (d) Apply a second layer in a usual spray application to get a thickness of 3 mils (0.003 in.) of dry film. (e) The basecoat and topcoat will fully dry together to make a rain resistant coating with these conditions: 1) Two hours of drying time with conditions of 50% relative humidity and 70°F (21.1°C). 2) The lipskin can be dried outside if there is no direct rain and the temperature is about 50°F (10.0°C). SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-008-F00 (8) Prepare the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411. NOTE: PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, can be used alone or for added exterior durability it can be over coated with Z6148 preservation topcoat. (a) Let the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C). (b) Fully mix the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, in the container. NOTE: If a mechanical paint shaker is used, the recommended mix time is 5 minutes. (c) Apply the basecoat with standard spray equipment. NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-009-F00 (9) Apply the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, to the lip skin. (a) Apply a 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment. (b) Let the first coat dry for one hour. NOTE: Drying can be accelerated by the circulation of warm air. (c) Apply a second 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer to achieve a total coating of 8 mils (0.008 in.) thickness. (d) Let the second coat dry for one hour. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-010-F00 (10) Prepare the PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412. (a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C). (b) Fully mix the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, in the container. NOTE: If a mechanical paint shaker is used, the recommended mix time is 5 minutes. 71-00-03 (c) Apply the topcoat with standard spray equipment. NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-011-F00 (11) Apply the PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, to the lip skin. (a) Make sure that the basecoat is dry (no gloss). (b) Apply a 2 mils (0.002 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment. (c) Allow to dry for two hours. NOTE: Full cure is achieved in 16 hours. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-012-F00 (12) Prepare the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410. (a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C). (b) Fully mix the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, in the container. (c) Apply the coating with standard spray equipment. NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly. SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-013-F00 (13) Apply the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, to the lip skin. (a) Apply a 2 mils (0.002 in.) - 3 mils (0.003 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment. (b) Allow to dry for 15 to 30 minutes. SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-004-F00 (14) Remove the masking material from the inner and outer barrels and the fan compartment.

H. Method 3 - Weekly Inspection for Corrosion and Cleaning

SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-004-F00 (1) If a protective coating is not available, do the following at least once (1) weekly. Daily inspection and cleaning is preferred. NOTE: Frequency of inspections will depend on the environmental condition that the airplane is stored in. Inspections and cleaning should be done at a frequency that ensures the lipskin does not have corrosive substance build up or prolonged moisture pooling on the lipskin surface. (a) With a soft low-lint cleaning cloth, G50933, moisten with alcohol, B00130, (preferred) or with de-ionized water, G02418, clean the nose cowl lipskin (TASK 20-10-34-110-802). (b) If corrosion is found, remove per the applicable SRM procedure. Make sure that the minimum thickness requirements per SRM are met.

I. Protective Coating Removal

SUBTASK 71-00-03-000-001-F00 (1) Do one of these steps to remove the protective coating from the lipskin: (a) If X20-18 compound, G51625, was used, perform the following steps: 71-00-03 1) Clean the lipskin with XS3 Aircraft Wash and XG5 Hard Surface Cleaner furnished from the X20-18 compound, G51625, vendor. NOTE: It is acceptable to perform general solvent cleaning per SOPM 20-30-03 as an alternative to the products recommended by Granitize. 2) Clean the surface until there are no signs of X20-18 compound, G51625, present on the lipskin. a) To detect the presence of X20-18 compound, G51625, on bare metal surfaces, perform one of the following: <1> Use Rulon J tape, G02356, to make a tab at the end. Firmly press the tape on a subject treated area and suspected untreated area. Pull the tab back slowly at a 90 degree angle to the surface. Noticeable ease in resistance will take place on a treated compared to the untreated surface. <2> Spray clean de-ionized water, G02418, on the surface. Moisture will bead up on a treated surface when compared to a non-treated surface. 3) Do this task if the aircraft will be put back into service: MMEL 30-03 (DDPG) Restoration - Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valves Inoperative, TASK 30-00-00-440-803. (b) If Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013/Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, PPG Z6160 coating, C50411/PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, or Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, was used, perform one of the following steps: 1) Use your hand to peel off the coating or use clean shop air. a) Refer to the coating manufacturer's recommendations for more details. 2) Do not use hand tools harder than the aluminum lipskin to prevent damage. CAUTION SCRIBE MARKS OR CUTS WHICH GO INTO THE METAL SURFACE OF THE LIP SKIN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE LIP SKIN. THE DAMAGE CAUSES LOSS OF FATIGUE LIFE OF THE METAL. (c) If necessary, use a hard resin phenolic scraper, STD-1064, (or equivalent), to help you remove the peelable coating with these conditions: 1) The tool does not go completely through the coating 2) The tool does not score or mar the lipskin 3) Use a scraper which has an adjustable depth of cut on the coating.

71-00-03-600-802-F00Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (Task Selection) ATA 71 · Task 600-802-F00

Task Description

4. Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (Task Selection)

A. General

(1) The purpose of this task is to permit you to select the applicable method to do the engine preservation. (2) This procedure is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).

B. Consumable Materials

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-002-F00 (1) From the time specification for the preservation tasks, select the applicable task to do the engine preservation: (a) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-804-F00. (b) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00. (c) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than Three Months (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-809-F00. (d) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine From One Month to One Year (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-043-F00 (2) These tasks give the instructions for the preservation, preservation renewal and depreservation for a serviceable and a non-serviceable engine. NOTE: For this procedure, a serviceable engine is defined as an engine that you can start. A non-serviceable engine is defined as an engine that cannot be started. (a) The preservation procedures for a serviceable engine gives the minimum recommended steps that are necessary to prevent these conditions: 1) Corrosion 2) Entry of unwanted material into the engine 3) The effects of the climate and weather conditions. (b) The preservation procedures for a non-serviceable engine gives the minimum recommended steps that are necessary if you cannot start the engine (c) The preservation renewal procedure, if it is permitted, gives the instructions for the renewal of the preservation time. (d) The depreservation procedure puts the installed engine back in operation. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-044-F00 (3) The preservation procedures are different for different periods of non-operational time, different types of preservation procedures, and if the power plant is serviceable or not serviceable. 71-00-03 (a) Power plant preservation is a flexible program that you can do, and must agree with the applicable weather and storage conditions. (b) More care is necessary for a program for power plants that are operational in high humidity or large temperature changes or near a salt water area, than for the power plants that are in drier climates or less bad weather conditions. 1) More care is necessary for power plants exposed to contaminants that promote corrosion (i.e deicing material). (c) You must do a schedule for the preservation programs for power plants that are not serviceable to do the preservation renewal procedures and monitor the schedule regularly to make sure that you did the necessary procedure before the expiration time. (d) In case of engine storage environmental humidity level that is higher than 70%, put desiccant bags in position with a humidity indicator in the inlet and the exhaust in order to monitor the humidity level. NOTE: The best condition for engine storage is to keep an environment with less than 70% relative humidity. 1) Make sure that the desiccant bags are not in contact with the engine hardware. 2) If necessary, use vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160] to locally protect the engine hardware. 3) Attach humidity indicator card (locally available) to monitor humidity level during the preservation period. 4) Make sure desiccant bags and humidity indicators are easily accessible. (e) When you use desiccants, you must do an inspection of them and change them regularly as applicable to the environmental conditions. NOTE: Installation of vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160] in inlet and exhaust can help to correctly seal engine flow path to make sure of desiccant bags effectiveness. NOTE: This will make sure that the desiccant gives good protection. (f) You must close the variable bleed valve (VBV) doors when you do the preservation and store the power plant. NOTE: Make sure that no unwanted material goes into the core engine inlet through the VBV's. (g) You must do the engine dry-out procedure after an engine had an in-flight shutdown, or when you do the long term preservation for a not serviceable engine.

71-00-03-600-803-F00Depreservation of an Engine On-Wing (Task Selection) ATA 71 · Task 600-803-F00

Task Description

5. Depreservation of an Engine On-Wing (Task Selection)

A. General

(1) The purpose of this task is to permit you to select the applicable method to do the engine depreservation. (2) This procedure is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).

B. References

Reference Title 71-00-00-700-821-F00 Dry Motor the Engine (P/B 201) 71-00-03

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Depreservation of an Engine On-Wing

SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-001-F00 (1) From the time specification for the depreservation tasks, select the applicable task to do the engine depreservation: CAUTION DO NOT DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE BEFORE YOU MAKE SURE THAT THE SPAR-VALVE CLOSED LIGHT (ON THE P5 OVERHEAD PANEL) STAYS BRIGHT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE APPLICABLE FOUR LOW PRESSURE LIGHTS ON THE P5 OVERHEAD PANEL ARE OFF . IF YOU DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE AND APPLICABLE LOW PRESSURE LIGHTS ARE ON, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE BEFORE YOU MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS FUEL PRESSURE TO THE FUEL PUMP INLET . THE FUEL PUMP AND HYDRO MECHANICAL UNIT ARE FUEL LUBRICATED. ZERO FUEL PRESSURE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FUEL PUMP AND HYDRO MECHANICAL UNIT . (a) If necessary on the engine to be dry motored, apply the boost pump pressure to the fuel pump inlet (TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00). (b) Do this task: Depreservation of an Engine, which was Preserved for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-808-F00. (c) Do this task: Depreservation of an Engine, which was Preserved for Not More Than Three Months (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-816-F00. (d) Do this task: Depreservation of an Engine, which was Preserved From One Month to Not More Than One Year (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-813-F00.

71-00-03-600-804-F00Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing) ATA 71 · Task 600-804-F00

Task Description

6. Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing)

A. General

(1) This task is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing). (2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable and a non-serviceable power plant.

B. References

Reference Title 24-11-21-200-801 Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) Air/Oil Cooler - Inspection/Check (P/B 201) 71-00-00-700-819-F00 Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop) (P/B 201) 71-00-00-800-807-F00 Start the Engine Procedure (Selection) (P/B 201) 71-00-03

C. Tools/Equipment

71-00-03-600-805-F00Preservation Renewal of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing) ATA 71 · Task 600-805-F00

Task Description

7. Preservation Renewal of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing)

A. General

(1) This procedure is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing). (2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable and a non-serviceable power plant. (3) Before engine operation, refer to Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00 for lipskin coating requirements during engine operation.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

C. Serviceable Power Plant

SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-004-F00 (1) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-804-F00. 71-00-03 (a) There is no limit on the number of times you can do this procedure. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-041-F00 (2) If applicable, apply protective coating to the inlet cowl lipskin after engine operation. Do this task: Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00.

D. Not Serviceable Power Plant

SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-005-F00 (1) You must do one of these procedures: (a) The preservation procedure of a non-serviceable power plant for not more than 1 month (TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00). NOTE: This will permit a preservation for not more than 30 days maximum from the time of the last engine operation or from the time the engine dry-out procedure was done. (b) The preservation procedure from one month to not more than one year for a non-serviceable power plant (TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00) if you will do the preservation renewal procedure.

71-00-03-600-807-F00Preservation Renewal of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing) ATA 71 · Task 600-807-F00

Task Description

9. Preservation Renewal of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing)

A. General

(1) This task is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing). (2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable and a non-serviceable power plant. (3) Before engine operation, refer to TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00 for lipskin coating requirements during engine operation.

B. References

Reference Title 36-11-02-400-801 Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation (P/B 401) 36-11-04-400-801 PRSOV Installation (P/B 401)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine

D. Serviceable Power Plant

SUBTASK 71-00-03-420-005-F00 (1) Before engine operation, if the Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV) and 5th stage bleed air check valve were removed and stored off the airplane, do the steps that follow: (a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct. (b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material. (c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801. (d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801. SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-002-F00 (2) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00. (a) If you do a 30–day preservation with engine idle run, this procedure can be renewed five (5) more times for a total duration of 180 days (TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00). (b) If you do a 30-day preservation with engine dry motor, this procedure can be renewed two (2) more times for a total duration of 90 days (TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00). NOTE: During engine idle run, both oil and fuel circulate through its system. During engine dry motor, the fuel does not circulate through the complete fuel system. (c) If the power plant will be kept for more than the subsequent 30 days, you must do one of these steps: 1) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than Three Months (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-809-F00. 2) Do the preservation of a serviceable engine from one month to one year (TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00). (d) If applicable, apply protective coating to the inlet cowl lipskin after engine operation, do this task: Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00. 71-00-03

E. Not Serviceable Power Plant

SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-007-F00 (1) A preservation renewal procedure is not permitted. SUBTASK 71-00-03-420-006-F00 (2) Operate the engine. (a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct. (b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material. (c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801. (d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-008-F00 (3) Do the preservation of a not serviceable engine from one month to one year (TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00).

Task Description

10. Depreservation of an Engine, which was Preserved for Not More Than One Month (Engine On- Wing)

A. General

(1) This task is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing). (2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable or a non-serviceable power plant.

B. References

SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-003-F00 (1) Remove the waterproof cover or engine bag (as applicable), vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], and desiccant bag, G02456 [CP2098]. (a) Make sure that you remove all of the moisture barrier tape, G02304, from the inlet and exhaust areas and that there is no unwanted material. (b) Make sure that you remove all vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], from the Variable Bleed Valve (VBV) bleed grills. 71-00-03 SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-007-F00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU FOLLOW THE LIPSKIN COATING PROCEDURES BEFORE AN ENGINE OPERATION. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW INSTRUCTIONS, THE COATING CAN MELT AND GO INTO THE ENGINE. THIS CAN CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE. (2) If not already done, remove the lipskin protective coating from the inlet cowl lipskin (TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00). SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-004-F00 (3) Make sure that all of the moisture barrier tape, G02304, is removed from the inlet and exhaust areas and that there is no unwanted material. SUBTASK 71-00-03-420-001-F00 (4) If the PRSOV and 5th stage bleed air check valve were removed and stored off of the airplane, do the steps that follow: (a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct. (b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material. (c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801. (d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801.

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 411 Engine 1 - Engine 421 Engine 2 - Engine F. Power Plant Preservation SUBTASK 71-00-03-210-007-F00 (1) If it is operator policy, examine and clean the IDG air/oil cooler (Reference Not Currently Available and TASK 24-11-21-200-801). NOTE: This check is recommended to prevent corrosion and cooler failure especially during operation in winter. SUBTASK 71-00-03-680-001-F00 (2) If it is not already done, do this task: Drain the Engine Oil, TASK 12-13-11-600-803. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-009-F00 (3) To fill the oil tank with preservation oil, do this task: Replenish the Engine Oil, TASK 12-13-11-600-801. (a) Fill the oil tank with 20 qt (19 l) of one of the preservation oils given below: 1) Engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 5 percent by volume of oil, D00664 [CP5067], or 2) Engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 7 percent by volume of additive, D00662 [CP5075]. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-048-F00 (4) Alternative method without oil tank draining: it is possible to skip step (2) above and prepare the mixture directly if you add the appropriate amount of corrosion preventive oil or corrosion inhibitor to the oil remaining in the tank. (a) In this case, add 1 qt (1 l) (resp. 1.4 qt (1.3 l)) of system corrosion preventive oil, D00664 [CP5067] (resp. corrosion preventive additive, D00662 [CP5075]), in the oil tank. (b) If it is necessary, partially drain the oil tank before you add the additive to prevent over servicing. (c) Complete the servicing with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], after you add the additive. NOTE: In this case, operating the engine at ground idle (step 5 below) is necessary and cannot be replaced by dry motoring. (d) If it is necessary, check oil level. SUBTASK 71-00-03-860-003-F00 (5) Perform idle run as follows: (a) Do this task: Start the Engine Procedure (Selection), TASK 71-00-00-800-807-F00. (b) Let the engine become stable for 15-20 minutes at the idle. (c) Do this task: Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop), TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00. 71-00-03 (d) When the engine cannot be operated at idle condition, dry motor the engine for 5 minutes, do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00. NOTE: This alternative is possible only if steps 2 and 3 have been completed (oil tank draining). (e) Refer to starter limitation to find out the number of dry motoring cycles to make sure of the total motoring time. NOTE: Preferred method to preserve the engine is by doing an idle run. During engine idle run, both oil and fuel circulate through its system. During engine dry motor, the fuel does not circulate through the complete fuel system. SUBTASK 71-00-03-710-003-F00 (6) If the VBV doors are open, close them. (a) Do this task: VBV Actuation System - Manual Operation, TASK 75-32-00-730-801-F00. SUBTASK 71-00-03-710-004-F00 (7) Put vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], on the VBV bleed grills. SUBTASK 71-00-03-020-003-F00 (8) If the APU or external air will be used to operate the ECS while the engine is preserved, it is recommended to remove the PRSOV and 5th stage bleed air check valve and store them off of the airplane, do these steps: (a) Remove the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Removal, TASK 36-11-04-000-801. (b) Remove the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve - Removal, TASK 36-11-02-000-801. NOTE: If removal of the fifth stage duct assembly was necessary to remove the bleed air check valve, it may also be stored off of the airplane. (c) Install an E-seal and a coupling with a blanking plate, SPL-18258, on the precooler upstream duct (Figure 206). 1) When the coupling is in place, tighten the coupling. a) Tighten the coupling nut to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb (14.1 N·m). b) Lightly tap the outer surface of the coupling with a rubber mallet, STD-3906. c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb (14.1 N·m). CAUTION DO NOT APPLY THE G00920 TAPE TO THE PAINTED SURFACES. THE TAPE IS HARD TO REMOVE. IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE SURFACES. (d) On the intersection manifold duct assembly and fifth stage duct assembly, cover the openings with a protective cover or use a barrier (plastic sheet) and tape. (e) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material. (f) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, or 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate tape, G51576, or tape, G00920. 1) If the fifth stage duct assembly is removed during removal of the bleed air check valve, cover the opening on the engine case (fifth stage port) with a barrier (plastic sheet) and tape. 71-00-03 2) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material. 3) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, or 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate tape, G51576, or tape, G00920. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-028-F00 (9) Put desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098], and humidity indicators in the inlet and exhausts of the engine to protect it from moisture as follows (PAGEBLOCK 71-00-03/201): NOTE: The best condition for engine stored is to keep an environment with less than 70% humidity. NOTE: Desiccant bags must be inspected/replaced at regular intervals depending on weather conditions. (a) Make sure that they are accessible for inspection/replacement while disturbing a minimum amount of protective material, do this task: Desiccant Bags Inspection Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-200-801-F00. (b) Mark the date on the humidity indicator tags. (c) Attach desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098], in the inlet and exhausts of the engine. 1) Make sure that they are not in contact with the engine hardware. (d) If it is necessary, use vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], to locally protect the engine hardware. SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-029-F00 (10) If it is necessary, seal the inlet and exhausts of the engine with vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], to protect it from moisture. (a) Attach vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], with moisture barrier tape, G02304. (b) To cover the inlet opening, apply the tape at the inner barrel ring (Figure 205). (c) Do not apply tape to or on the inlet cowl lipskin. SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-009-F00 (11) Put the adequate protective cover that follows: (a) If the engine is stored off-wing, put a waterproof cover over the whole engine. 1) Make sure that it is tightly fitted to the engine. (b) If the engine is stored on-wing, put a waterproof cover over the whole powerplant. 1) Make sure that it is tightly fitted to the powerplant. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DRAIN MASTS ARE CLEAR OF BLOCKAGE. BLOCKED DRAINS CAN CAUSE WATER TO COLLECT IN THE THRUST REVERSER. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT . 2) If not possible, as an alternative, install the kit, COM-1501 (preferred), or inlet cover, COM-1516, and exhaust plug, SPL-18121 (alternate), to prevent fan windmilling and to prevent Foreign Object Damage (FOD). NOTE: The exhaust plug, SPL-18121, installs to the exhaust and bypass of the engine. NOTE: The engine exhaust cover, SPL-1517, and engine fan reverser plug, SPL-14648, are alternative covers to the exhaust plug, SPL-18121. 71-00-03 CAUTION DO NOT APPLY THE G00920 TAPE TO THE PAINTED SURFACES. THE TAPE IS HARD TO REMOVE. IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE SURFACES. (c) If the engine inlet and exhaust tool covers are not available, use a barrier (plastic sheet) and tape. (d) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material. (e) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, or 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate tape, G51576, or tape, G00920. 1) When you use a plastic sheet for the exhaust cover, make sure that the drain holes or tubes are clear of the cover. 2) When you use a plastic sheet, for the inlet cover, do the steps that follow: a) Use lint-free cloth, G00834, and solvent, B00666, to wipe the area where the tape is used. b) Cut an approximately 60 in. (1.5 m) diameter circle from a plastic sheet. c) Put tape on the circle on the FWD edge of the acoustic panel behind the lipskin. d) Apply a minimum of 3 overlap layers of tape around the perimeter of the inlet acoustic panel. e) Do not place plastic or tape over the lipskin or cover the lipskin with plastic. f) Apply the tape across the diameter of the circular sheet to reduce the pillowing of the plastic sheeting. SUBTASK 71-00-03-970-003-F00 (12) Attach a tag to the power plant that shows that the oil system preservation was done with preservation oil. (a) Include the date of the preservation procedure.
